From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Award

| The ReFrame Stamp |
| --- |
| [![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/5/5f/ReFrame_Stamp_for_Gender-Balanced_Production_certification_mark.png/250px-ReFrame_Stamp_for_Gender-Balanced_Production_certification_mark.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ReFrame_Stamp_for_Gender-Balanced_Production_certification_mark.png) |
| Awarded for | Recognition of gender-balanced film and television productions featuring women in key roles |
| Country | [United States](link_2) |
| Presented by | [ReFrame](link_3) |
| First award | June 8, 2018 |
| Website | [https://www.reframeproject.org/stamp](https://www.reframeproject.org/stamp) |

**The ReFrame Stamp for Gender-Balanced Production** certification is awarded by [ReFrame](link_3) to corporations and media that show progress toward [gender equality](link_4) and greater representation of women in key roles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-2)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 5: [icon]](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg/20px-Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg)This section **needs expansion**. You can help by [adding missing information](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=). _(March 2019)_

On June 8, 2018, the ReFrame Stamp program was launched to promote and recognize gender-balanced productions in film and television based on data from [IMDb](link_5)Pro on how many women are involved in a production in front of and behind the camera.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-3) On September 26, the Stamp program expanded to include submissions for TV shows and movies from cable and streaming platforms.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-4) ReFrame entered into a partnership in February 2020 with Delta Air Lines in which two in-flight channels dedicated to films and television programs respectively with the ReFrame Stamp would be featured.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-5) The ReFrame Movie Channel launched with 29 initial offerings including [_Wonder Woman_](link_6), [_The Hate U Give_](link_7), _[Ocean's 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean [link_8]'s\_8 "Ocean's 8")_, and [_Lady Bird_](link_9). The ReFrame Show Channel's initial releases included [_Supergirl_](link_10), [_Empire_](link_11), [_How to Get Away With Murder_](link_12), and [_Better Things_](link_13). These offerings were planned to cycle on a monthly basis with additions in each lineup.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-6)

## Submission process

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Submission process")]

Qualifying films must be distributed either theatrically or via streaming, while TV shows are counted in relation to the calendar for the [Emmy Awards](link_14). Films and television which are not considered top 100 grossing projects may be considered through a rolling open call via a manual submission process.

During any given submission period, the individual entering the information regarding the feature film which has been distributed theatrically or via streaming must utilize the Narrative Feature, Animated Feature, or Television submission form. As of 2019, information provided in each submission must include the project title, year of release, studio (or platform), distributor, and contact information for both a production and studio/distributor representative. The submission must specify the positions of each woman involved in qualifying areas for consideration, as well as whether each of those specified is a [person of color](link_15).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-8) Appeals for ReFrame Stamp submissions are reviewed using an independent panel and may be submitted via email.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-9)

## Criteria

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Criteria")]

Based on a points system, [narrative films](link_16) and animated films[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-FilmStampCriteria-10) and TV programs[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-11) must achieve four points within the eight defined qualifying categories with at least two points in the categories of female director, writer, and lead. Double points are awarded for women of color in important positions. Screen time analysis is done with the [Geena Davis Inclusion Quotient (GD-IQ)](link_17)[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_],[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-12) while points are calculated by an algorithm and given to the films or TV programs that meet the requirements. After the stamp is awarded, a logo is added to the end credits.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-:02-13) The criteria are subject to change accordingly with the evolving industry.

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Film")]

*   Female lead (Top 1 slot listed on the call sheet) 
    *   1 point for a female lead
    *   2 points for a female lead of color

*   Female co-lead (Top 2-5 slots on the call sheet) 
    *   1 point for a female lead
    *   2 points for a female lead of color

*   Female representation on screen 
    *   1 point when 50% of the screen time is female
    *   2 points when 25% of the screen time is females of color

*   Female director 
    *   1 point for a female director
    *   2 points for a female director of color

*   Female writer 
    *   1 point for a credited female writer
    *   2 points for a credited female writer of color

*   Female producer 
    *   1 point for a female producer
    *   2 points for a female producer of color

*   50% of department heads are female 
    *   1 point for 50% female department heads
    *   2 points for 25% female department heads of color

*   50% of crew members 
    *   1 point for 50% female crew
    *   2 points for 25% female crew of color

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Television")]

*   Female lead (Top 1 slot listed on the call sheet) 
    *   1 point for a female lead
    *   2 points for a female lead of color

*   Female season regulars (Top 2-5 slots on the call sheet) 
    *   1 point if 50% of season regulars are female
    *   2 points if 25% of season regulars are females of color

*   Female showrunner 
    *   1 point for a female showrunner
    *   2 points for a female showrunner of color

*   Female writing staff 
    *   1 point if 50% of writing staff are female writers (per season)
    *   2 points if 25% of writing staff are female writers of color (per season)

The ReFrame Stamp is awarded annually to narrative Feature Films and Television that hire women, those who are non-binary and/or gender non-conforming, and trans people of all genders in key roles across the production. The ReFrame Stamp is awarded to **narrative Feature Films** and **scripted Television Shows**.

The following types of media are **not eligible** for the ReFrame Stamp at this time:

Web Series  
Short Films  
Branded Content/Commercials  
Music Videos  
Documentaries or Non-Fiction/Unscripted Content  
Reality or Competition Series

The Stamp criteria were developed with ReFrame Ambassadors, producers, and other industry experts. Accounting for key decision-makers across the production, the ReFrame Stamp criteria ensures a comprehensive approach to evaluating hiring practices and crew makeup.

Ready to get your production ReFrame Stamped? Apply now! If your production qualifies, gather all necessary documents and information, and click below to apply.

[![Image 4](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58a204bfb3db2b8884d8c01f/c2b6c922-c6cb-405d-9532-a1b3f3e8fe5e/DOMESTIC+FEATURE.png)](https://reframeproject.org/stamp/film [link_10])

[![Image 5](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58a204bfb3db2b8884d8c01f/222b2f60-dbd8-4fe2-8e73-b61f03a5e15c/TELEVISION.png)](https://www.reframeproject.org/stamp-criteria-tv [link_11])

![Image 6](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58a204bfb3db2b8884d8c01f/2cc0e02d-64e5-4da7-b685-0b8b0082ef04/Heading+%281%29.png)

![Image 7](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58a204bfb3db2b8884d8c01f/33249d99-97e8-4ace-8620-825406ecb27b/2025-26+ReFrame+TV+Report+Cover.png)

![Image 8](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58a204bfb3db2b8884d8c01f/5c2daa4c-ceeb-4aea-b6e5-1a75a6856dd6/Stamp_Dividing+Banners.png)

ReFrame’s annual report on Gender & Hiring in TV will be released in October 2026, continuing the organization’s yearly analysis of equity in the TV industry.

**Key Findings:**

*   **Screens are becoming less diverse:**There were only 39 women, trans, or nonbinary people in leading roles in this year’s series, down five from last year and the fewest in seven years. The decrease was even more significant for qualifying candidates of color in supporting on-screen roles.

*   **Limited progress in above-the-line roles:**Representation in above-the-line roles has been fairly steady since the 2022-23 season, though generally representation of women in creative decision-making roles is lower now than it was four years ago.

*   **Streaming continues to dominate the TV landscape (and gender-balanced hiring):**87% of the most popular shows of the year were streaming exclusives. Almost half (44%) of those series demonstrated overall gender-balanced hiring.

*   **Gender-balanced series were more likely to be renewed, and less likely to be cancelled:**Of the 11 shows cancelled after their 2025-2026 season, only 4 cancellations were Stamped, compared to 7 cancelled non-Stamped series.

American non-profit organisation

**ReFrame** (also known as **ReFrame Project**; formerly known as the **Systemic Change Project**) is an American non-profit organization founded by [Women in Film LA](link_3)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-1) and the [Sundance Institute](link_4) together with over 50 leaders and influencers in Hollywood, with the goal of providing research, support, and a practical framework to its partner companies[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-:1-3) to give them a way to "mitigate bias during the creative decision-making and hiring process, celebrate successes, and measure progress toward a more gender-representative industry on all levels".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-4) Alison Emilio serves as the director.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-:0-5)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ReFrame&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The Systemic Change Project, a joint venture between Women in Film and the Sundance Institute,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-:1-3) originated from a secret meeting of 44 Hollywood leaders to address the gender parity issue in the industry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-6) From the Systemic Change Project, ReFrame was founded by a group of ReFrame Ambassabors, active male and female leaders across the entertainment industry ranging from studio heads to guild representatives, ReFrame seeks to use a developed research-based action plan to promote gender parity, inclusivity, diversity, and increase the presence of women in the media industry.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-8)

## Programs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ReFrame&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Programs")]

### 14-Point Culture Change and Production Roadmap

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ReFrame&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 14-Point Culture Change and Production Roadmap")]

Building on existing diversity programs, the roadmap provides tools, training, and practices tailored to entertainment executives and creative teams to address the systemic barriers in the creative and financial aspects of the business.

### ReFrame Rise Directors Program

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ReFrame&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: ReFrame Rise Directors Program")]

On June 12, 2019, the ReFrame Rise Directors Program was announced as a mentorship program. It was an industry-wide two-year sponsorship that identified promising female directors poised to lead studio features and TV projects, and provided them with endorsement and support. Those selected for ReFrame Rise received complimentary IMDbPro memberships.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-10)

### ReFrame Stamp

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ReFrame&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: ReFrame Stamp")]

Main article: [The ReFrame Stamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp "The ReFrame Stamp")

The ReFrame Stamp is a distinction awarded to film and TV productions that satisfy predetermined criteria with a large number of women in key roles in front and behind the camera as actresses, members of the production, and department heads. Criteria for the award includes having a female protagonist with top billing, female characters with a lot of screen time, female directors and screenwriters with additional recognition towards women of color in main roles.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-11) The stamp is awarded based on the number of points fulfilled by the aforementioned criteria. After a film or television program is awarded the stamp, a logo is added to the end credits.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame#cite_note-:0-5)

_**The Hate U Give**_ is a 2018 American [coming-of-age](link_22)[teen](link_23)[drama film](link_24) co-produced and directed by [George Tillman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr [link_2]. "George Tillman Jr."), and written by [Audrey Wells](link_3), who died a day before the film's release. Based on the [2017 young adult novel](link_4) by [Angie Thomas](link_5), the film stars [Amandla Stenberg](link_8) as a high school student navigating the fallout of her friend's death in a police shooting. The supporting cast includes [Drew Starkey](link_12), [Regina Hall](link_9), [Russell Hornsby](link_10), [Lamar Johnson](link_25), [KJ Apa](link_11), [Sabrina Carpenter](link_13), [Common](link_14), and [Anthony Mackie](link_15).

The project was announced in March 2016, and casting took place from August to September 2017. [Principal photography](link_26) began that same September in [Atlanta](link_27) and wrapped in November. Originally, [Kian Lawley](link_28) was cast in Apa's role, but he was fired after footage of him using racial slurs resurfaced. Apa was brought in to reshoot Lawley's scenes in April 2018.

_The Hate U Give_ premiered at the [2018 Toronto International Film Festival](link_29) on September 7, 2018,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hate_U_Give_(film)#cite_note-5) and was released in the United States on October 5, by [20th Century Fox](link_20).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hate_U_Give_(film)#cite_note-6) The film received critical acclaim and grossed $34.9 million worldwide on a $23 million budget. Stenberg's performance earned several accolades, including the [NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Actress in a Motion Picture](link_30) and a [Critics' Choice Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics [link_31]'_Choice_Movie_Awards "Critics' Choice Movie Awards") nomination for [Best Young Performer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics [link_31]'_Choice_Movie_Award_for_Best_Young_Performer "Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Young Performer").

2017 film by Greta Gerwig

This article is about the 2017 film. For the 1927 film, see [The Ladybird (film)](link_3).

_**Lady Bird**_ is a 2017 American [coming-of-age](link_24)[comedy drama](link_25) film written and directed by [Greta Gerwig](link_4) in her solo directorial debut, starring [Saoirse Ronan](link_8), [Laurie Metcalf](link_9), [Tracy Letts](link_10), [Lucas Hedges](link_11), [Timothée Chalamet](link_12), [Beanie Feldstein](link_13), [Stephen McKinley Henderson](link_14), and [Lois Smith](link_15). Set in [Sacramento, California](link_26) during the early 2000s, it focuses on a high school senior who has a turbulent relationship with her mother.

**ReFrame Rise™** is a comprehensive and customized two-year program designed by ReFrame, a Women in Film and Sundance Institute collaboration, to accelerate high-level, sustainable advancement for mid-career women, nonbinary and trans directors and cinematographers. ReFrame Rise is supported by Netflix.   
  
The program provides Rise fellows with introductions to industry sponsors and offers participation at in-person filmmaker events, including the Sundance Film Festival; closed-door Q&As with industry leaders on relevant mid-career topics; and career strategy sessions to support fellows with publicity, materials development and pitching. The 2025-2026 ReFrame Rise cohort is comprised of 11 women and nonbinary filmmakers specficially based in Los Angeles, to maximize in-person community and industry relationship building, as well as to support LA film workers at this time.

[](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1170520/bio/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm)

Sophie Hyde is a founding member of Closer Productions and social impact company The Unquiet Collective.  
  
In 2022, Sophie directed Emma Thompson in the BAFTA and Golden Globe nominated comedy Good Luck To You, Leo Grande.  
  
Her debut feature drama 52 Tuesdays won the Directing Award at Sundance and the Crystal Bear at the Berlinale. She directed and produced feature comedy Animals based on the novel of the same name by Emma Jane Unsworth.  
  
Sophie's television work includes F*!#ing Adelaide for ABC Australia, and The Hunting for SBS.  
  
She co-directed and produced feature documentary Life in Movement which won the Australian documentary prize at Sydney Film Festival.  
  
Sophie believes strongly in nurturing the voices of other filmmakers and therefore also works as a producer and EP on various projects including feature documentaries Shut Up Little Man! An Audio Misadventure, Sam Klemke's Time Machine, In My Blood It Runs and the Netflix original documentary The Dreamlife of Georgie Stone.  
  
Her latest film Jimpa, starring Olivia Colman and John Lithgow, is set for release in 2025.

# ReFrame Report on 

# Gender & Hiring in Film 2025 1 0 0 % O F P R O J E C T S C A N E A R N T H E S T A M P 

This year’s analysis captured the first significant drop in gender-balanced projects in six years, and found that the number of qualifying directors helming films in the Top 100 fell for the second consecutive year. Whereas last year’s drop in qualifying directors–which includes women, nonbinary and gender non-conforming people, and trans people of all genders–did not impact the overall volume of films that were gender-balanced, this year’s drop did correspond with a decrease for gender-balanced projects. 

## ReFrame Stamp Count & Qualifying Directors Year Over Year  *In 2025, 26 of the IMDbPro Top 100 Films Earned the ReFrame Stamp 

* From 2017-2019, ReFrame exclusively analyzed annual lists of the top-grossing box office films. In 2020, ReFrame’s data set shifted to the IMDbPro Top 100 Films, a metric based on the page views of the more than 250 million monthly worldwide visitors to IMDb, and includes films that were released theatrically, films released exclusively by streamers and films with a limited theatrical release. The decision to move to analyzing the ‘most popular’ films was motivated by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the box office and the opportunity to review projects encompassing all major studios, distributors and means of distribution. 

ReFrame’s criteria is designed to make gender equity achievable for all films, regardless of the gender identity of its creator or characters. 

1I N T R O D U C T I O N 

Materialists Materialists 

Since 2017, ReFrame, the gender equity coalition founded by WIF (formerly Women in Film Los Angeles) and the Sundance Institute, has collaborated with IMDbPro to identify which films from the year’s 100 most popular releases meet ReFrame Stamp criteria for gender-balanced production. This year’s ReFrame Report on Gender & Hiring in Film found the fewest gender-balanced projects in six years. Only 11 women directed films on the 2025 Top 100 list, down nearly half from a peak of 20 in 2023. A further breakdown of this year’s data, as well as key findings and highlights, follows. To learn more about the ReFrame Stamp, visit reframeproject.org/stamp. 

ReFrame Report on Gender & Hiring in Film 2025 I N T R O D U C T I O N A Year of Rollback: The Lowest Number of Gender-Balanced Films in Six Years 2I N T R O D U C T I O N 

Victoria Mahoney and Cast Victoria Mahoney and Cast on the set of on the set of The Old Gaurd 2 The Old Gaurd 2 (BTS) (BTS) 

A N O T E F R O M R E F R A M E ’ S F O U N D E R S 

“The ReFrame Stamp was designed as a stepping stone, with moderate measures for substantive inclusion of women, nonbinary and trans people in key roles in front of and behind the camera to qualify as gender-balanced. This was meant as a floor, not a ceiling, on our way to inclusive hiring. The fact that even this baseline remains a minority achievement is alarming. Instead of raising the bar, we're now seeing productions falling below it. This is not progress. This is a reversal." 

> - Cathy Schulman, Oscar-winning Producer, WIF President Emeritas and founder of Welle Entertainment & Keri Putnam, Producer and former Sundance Institute CEO

A D E E P E R D I V E O N G E N D E R A N D E M P L O Y M E N T H I S T O R Y I N F I L M 

For an even more comprehensive look at historical employment of women in the film industry, ReFrame recommends the 28th annual edition of "The Celluloid Ceiling: Employment of Behind-the-Scenes Women on Top Grossing U.S. Films in 2025" by Dr. Martha Lauzen, which examines gender and hiring in key roles across an even broader set of films and has tracked women’s employment and credits on the top 250 domestic-grossing films for the past 28 years.

This chart breaks out Stamped films into three groups by their reported production budget levels: those with reported production budgets under 30 million dollars, those between 30 and 100 million dollars, and those budgeted at 100 million dollars or more. Over the past four years, the proportion of films at the highest budget level of $100M+ has increased significantly–nearly ten percent. A recent feature in The Wrap unpacked the significance women can have at the box office, both as creators and consumers: “Not only is Hollywood finding success in making films for and by women, but a steadier clip of these films in theaters is providing exhibitors with a healthier balance sheet,” which “proves that when Hollywood caters to an underserved audience, they more often than not show up.”

> * Excludes films whose budgets have not been publicly disclosed.

K E Y F I N D I N G S : P R O D U C T I O N B U D G E T S 

This graph displays average budgets for Stamped and non-Stamped films year-over-year. Last year, production budgets for both sets of films fell about $10M, but this year Stamped films regained much of that ground. Stamped budgets rose significantly from $53M in 2024 to $62M in 2025; non-Stamped budgets rose slightly from $65M in 2024 to $67M in 2025. This growth in Stamped film budgets also narrowed the gap in average budgets from $12M last year to only $5M this year. 

# Production Budgets Rebound... Slightly 

The Future of Film is Representative – Gen Alpha and Gen Z Care About Authenticity on the Big Screen 

According to "Teens & Screens 2025", a new report from UCLA’s Center for Scholars and Storytellers, “seeing a new movie in theatres” is the top-ranked activity for adolescents currently between 10 and 24 years old for the second year in a row, beating video games, streaming and sports, among other entertainment types. Along with the drive to keep the theatrical experience alive, these generations have also made “authenticity and values non-negotiable” and demand “authentic representation that goes beyond token gestures” on screen, according to recent market research. 

Elio Elio 

ReFrame Report on Gender & Hiring in Film 2025 S T R E A M I N G - F I R S T S T R A T E G Y S U P P O R T S A G E N D E R - B A L A N C E D B R E A K O U T 5ReFrame Stamped Films in Every Release Style 

This chart displays the proportion of films in each distribution segment – streaming, theatrical and limited theatrical – that earned the ReFrame Stamp. Beginning with last year’s reporting on the films of 2024, a significant volume of films employed a hybrid release strategy, appearing for a limited time in theatres or releasing in theatres and on streaming simultaneously. In a few cases, including Netflix’s breakout KPOP: Demon Hunters , films succeeded with at-home viewers and gained such popularity on streaming that they were exhibited theatrically after their initial streaming release. 

This year, one gender-balanced project broke records on multiple charts by first becoming Netflix’s most-watched animated film–then, even further, becoming the most popular Netflix film of all time. The film’s streaming success prompted a unique strategy among this year’s limited theatrical releases, travelling to the big screen months after its initial wildly successful streaming release. The strategy paid off: it gave Netflix their first No. 1 title at the box office. Check out this year’s Anatomy of a Stamped Film on page 12 for a closer look at the points this film earned to receive the ReFrame Stamp. Another accolade for this hit that maximized both streaming views and box office results? It also earned more points to qualify for its Stamp than any other film reviewed in 2025–a gender-balanced WIN!

"KPop Demon Hunters would simply not exist without women. And there were sooooo many women in every different department. Women producers, executives, writers, directors, animators, artists, actors, singers, etc. more than any other project we’ve ever worked on. And look how it turned out! The proof is in the pudding, everybody. Honestly, no one should make a movie without a TON of women involved EVER again." 

KPop Demon Hunters KPop Demon Hunters 

- Danya Jimenez and Hannah McMechan, Co-Writers KPop Demon Hunters 

ReFrame Report on Gender & Hiring in Film 2025 6The Top The Middle The Bottom 

This year, Netflix was the only company meeting 50% in its volume of Stamped films in the Top 100. Though a slight decrease from the 56.25% it held in 2024, Netflix is a consistent leader year-over-year for inclusive hiring and gender-balanced projects. It is followed by Lionsgate, which holds the ReFrame Stamp for 40% of its projects this year, its highest volume since 2020. Five companies–Amazon MGM Studios (which includes releases from Amazon Prime Video & Amazon MGM Studios), Disney (which includes releases from Walt Disney Studios and 20th Century Studios), NBC Universal (which includes releases from Universal Pictures and Focus Features), Paramount Pictures and Sony (which includes releases from Sony Pictures Classics, Sony Pictures Entertainment and Screen Gems)--fall in the middle with Stamped films comprising 22.2%, 35.71%, 20%, 20% and 22.2% of their 2025 slates, respectively. Three companies had less than 15% of their films in the Top 100 meet the mark for gender-balanced production, and one company had none at all. A24, Warner Bros. Discovery (which includes releases from Warner Bros. Pictures) and the Independent category (which this year includes one release each from AMC, Bleeker Street Media, MUBI*, AMC’s Shudder and Vertical Entertainment, and two releases from Neon) had 12.5%, 11.11% and 14.29% Stamped films, respectively. Of the three films released by Apple in the Top 100, there were no Stamped releases.   

> *MUBI’s DIE MY LOVE was the only Stamped film released by a distributor in the independent category.
> C O M P A N Y R E P O R T C A R D

C O M P A N Y R E P O R T C A R D ReFrame Stamped Releases by Company in the Top 100 ReFrame Report on Gender & Hiring in Film 2025 7Declining Diversity in Lead and Co-Lead Roles Qualifying Leads Qualifying Co-Leads O N - S C R E E N R E P R E S E N T A T I O N 

Diverse on-camera performers have gained significant ground over the past eight years of ReFrame reporting, often a bellwether of increasing inclusion in the film industry. However, 2025 exhibits notable decreases for women and no inclusion of nonbinary and transgender lead and co-lead performers. Last year, lead roles portrayed by women in the Top 100 Films reached 51%, the highest recorded by this report, and for the first time included one film starring a transgender performer. This year’s Top 100 Films displayed a pronounced reduction: lead roles held by a qualifying performer decreased from 51 to 39 roles, a reduction of 23.5% and the greatest drop in year-over-year representation recorded by this report. Qualifying performers who are also people of color decreased from 17 to 7, a reduction of 58.8%, which is both the largest drop and the fewest in total recorded in eight years. 

U N E Q U A L R E P R E S E N T A T I O N : P E R F O R M E R S O V E R 4 5 

With great insights on intersectional representation including gender and beyond, check out the most recent release from USC Annenberg, "Inequality across 1,900 Popular Films: Examining Gender, Race/Ethnicity & Age of Leads/Co Leads From 2007 to 2025". This study examined the representation of age in the top films of 2025, and found that while 30 of the Top 100 Films included roles for men 45 years or older, there were only four such roles portrayed by women and no roles for women of color over 45 years old. Among co-leading roles, the four most prominent or featured performers in supporting roles in each film, there was also a decrease in representation. Following two years in which 97 of the Top 100 Films included at least one qualifying performer as a co-lead, this year there were only 91 films that included women among their co-leads.

Women directed 11 films in this year’s Top 100, a decrease from last year’s 14, and the fewest recorded since 2019 when 12 women directed films on the list. None of these films were directed by trans or nonbinary people, but did include six women of color, a slight increase from last year’s five and comprising more than half of the women who directed Top 100 Films. While last year, all women with films in the Top 100 qualified for the Stamp, this year only nine of the 11 did. 

C A N P E R F O R M E R S T U R N T H E T I D E ? 

Entertainment news publication The Ankler released a profile focused on the dearth of women in 2025’s slate: in "Female Directors and Hollywood’s Grim #MeToo Reality", Richard Rushfield examines progress for women directors over the last 10 years, concluding that “while we were never doing all that much better than pre-#MeToo, in 2025, the state of female feature directors is definitely as bad, if not a little worse.” In considering solutions, he proposes top on-camera talent “demand to work with female directors.” For example, Nicole Kidman, who notably pledged in 2017 that she would work with a female director every 18 months to increase representation above the line, has worked with women directors on three of her last eight films. “Now is the time when we lean on the knowledge that progress is not linear. And now more than ever, it’s important that we support one another with the understanding that we are in a period where we need each other’s support. Without Kristin Burr, I would not have been chosen to direct Freakier Friday. Without the countless women and men behind the scenes and in front of the camera fighting for the importance of female directors, it would be too easy to maintain the status quo. But there are a vast amount of supporters doing the work of making sure we do not roll back the progress we have made. As an Industry and as film lovers - we all want and deserve the breadth of films only a diverse group of creators behind the camera can bring.” 

- Nisha Ganatra, Director Freakier Friday

This year, films crediting women as writers among the Top 100 saw a slight rebound from last year’s 23 to 27, and included six women of color who were credited as writers on five films. While this is a slight increase for qualifying writers of color from last year’s three, representation has a long way to go. In the past eight years, the greatest number of Top 100 films crediting women of color as their writers has never exceeded nine. This year captured 55 women credited as producers or receiving the p.g.a mark on the Top 100 Films, the most women recorded in this role since 2019. Despite representation for women in a producing role measuring between 40% and 56% among the Top 100 Films across the past seven years, there are few women of color among them. This year, there were six films with women of color credited as producers on top-performing films; as with qualifying screenwriters of color, the maximum number of women producers of color recorded over the eight-year period was nine. “Female audiences are driving huge numbers at the box office. No one understands this better than my partners at Lionsgate, Pretty Dangerous, and Hidden Pictures. Movies for women, with complicated female protagonists, often get framed as underdog stories or sold as sleeper hits in success. But the reality is that women are controlling the purse strings for the majority households and are wildly under-served by the annual slate of movies. We were so lucky to have a chain of women linking arms to champion our movie from a place of personal passion."

Variety’s "The Movie Theater Comeback That Wasn’t: Why 2025 Was Such a Dud for Struggling Cinemas" unpacks the theatrical releases of 2025, examining their content and concluding that “more diversified content would help insulate theatres from some Hollywood changes.” Mike Sherrill, Alamo Drafthouse CEO, is quoted as saying that he “would like to think that studios and distributors are looking at the trends and seeing that original, fresh stories are working” – and meet audience demand for authentic, representative big screen storytelling. 

- Laura Fischer, Producer The Housemaid 

G E N D E R D I V E R S I T Y O N S C R E E N ? N O T T H I S Y E A R . 

This year’s Top 100 Films did not include any nonbinary or transgender performers among all cast appearing in leading and co-leading roles. Across 15 behind-the-camera roles per film on 100 films (1,500 roles), there were only three gender-diverse individuals captured in this year’s analysis, all in the role of intimacy coordinator and employed across four films. 

ReFrame Report on Gender & Hiring in Film 2025 10 

The following graph displays the year-over-year breakdown for below-the-line roles. As the overall volume of gender-balanced projects drops, representation in most below-the-line roles shows little or no change. This year’s most significant increase in below-the-line representation is in the role of production designer; in the Top Films of 2025 there were 37 films with women in this role, the highest volume yet recorded and a 42% increase from last year’s 26. 

## Gender Diversity in Key Below the Line Roles Over Time K E Y R O L E S : B E L O W T H E L I N E W O M E N O F C O L O R B E H I N D T H E C A M E R A 

While some roles saw specific gains for women of color among this year’s Top 100 Films—including aforementioned directors of photography and visual effects supervisors, a role which included three women of color this year, but had none last year—the hiring of women and gender-diverse people of color has never exceeded 5% in the majority of below-the-line roles. The exception is costume designers, a role where women have substantial representation and have included as many as 12 women of color in a year’s Top 100, and production designers, who peaked with six films employing women of color in the role in 2021. This indicates continued, significant barriers to employment and leadership roles for women, nonbinary and transgender people of color in entertainment.

A secret meeting of 44 top Hollywood movers and shakers — among them producers Paula Wagner and Mike De Luca, HBO Films president Len Amato and director Catherine Hardwicke — has come up with a four-point plan “for solving the gender parity issue that plagues Hollywood.” The two-day meeting, held October 14-15 but only now coming to light, was hosted by [Women in Film](https://deadline.com/tag/women-in-film/) and the [Sundance Institute](https://deadline.com/tag/sundance-institute/) at the Pacific Design Center in LA.

The plan includes gender bias training, a sponsor/protégé program,an ambassador program to spread the word that the industry is serious about change and a “gender parity stamp” to be placed on films and TV shows that embrace gender equality.

“We are at an economic, social and cultural tipping point and sustainable change is within reach,” said Cathy Schulman, president of Women in Film Los Angeles. “The time to act is now. Hollywood is surprisingly late in coming to this party and this is the time for conversion.”

Said Keri Putnam, Executive Director of Sundance Institute: “The time is right to gather industry leadership and start to address these obstacles.The commitment from participants makes me believe that the industry is ready to explore real, tangible solutions that create more opportunities for women.”

The four-point plan:

• Advocate “Unconscious Bias” training across the industry. Leaders in other businesses have determined that unconscious bias creates blind spots and leads to missed market opportunities, and also hinders access to valuable consumer segments limiting profits. Creating more content for women and people of color is not only about equality; it also makes good business sense. An expert Unconscious Bias educator will be selected to work with executives and creatives across the industry.

### Watch on Deadline

● Develop and launch a Gender Parity Stamp to recognize films and television shows — as well as production companies, networks and studios — that show measurable progress to achieving gender equity. Mirrored on the successful work by LGBT advocates and the PGA’s producer mark, this recognition for positive progress will be a visible identifier for companies that have prioritized equal gender hiring practice and have financed or supported business opportunities for women in front of and behind the camera.

● Sponsor/Protégé Program. This high-level pilot program will identify talented early-to-mid career female film and TV directors for a year-long training and fellowship program, and pair them with advocates across the industry who will actively help them move to the next level. While many individual companies have training programs, this unique program will enable the protégé to work across different networks, studios and agencies. With the support and participation of executives across the industry, this program will highlight women selected by a panel of leaders and assure they have the tools, relationships, and exposure to launch and sustain their careers.

● Ambassadors from the industry leaders at the meeting will spread the word about the solutions to studios, networks and agencies. Crucially, the participants have committed to staying involved in the project and will enlist an ever-growing group of advocates to work inside their organizations on articulating the business case for making changes in culture and practices to hire more women and people of color.

The participants included industry leaders – both men and women — from the studios, networks, distributors, guilds and agencies, as well as high-profile writers, directors and producers (see the full list below). They began by reviewing the obstacles women face in Hollywood, as identified by four years of research conducted by the Sundance Institute/Women in Film Los Angeles and the USC Annenberg School of Communication and Journalism. The meeting concluded with proposals to remove those barriers and to help female filmmakers move up the industry ladder.

One of the participants, Erik Feig, co-president of Lionsgate, said: “As someone who has professionally and creatively greatly benefited from women as protagonists, directors, producers, writers, fellow executives and audiences, gender parity has always seemed like the most win-win goal for anyone in the entertainment industry so getting behind this objective was a very easy decision for me.”

The two-day think tank was led by Carolyn Buck Luce and Rob Evans, the expert facilitation team at Imaginal Labs., who have worked with senior executives from 40 of the Fortune 100 companies and designed breakthrough strategies for women’s advancement with such companies as Google, Goldman Sachs, Time Warner, NBC Universal, Bloomberg and Intel.

**George Tillman Jr.** (born January 26, 1969) is an American filmmaker.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-1)

Tillman directed the films _[Soul Food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Food\_(film) "Soul Food (film)")_ (1997) and _[Men of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men\_of\_Honor "Men of Honor")_ (2000). He is also the producer of _[Soul Food: The Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Food:\_The\_Series "Soul Food: The Series")_ on television and the four films in the [_Barbershop_ series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbershop_(film_series) "Barbershop (film series)"): _[Barbershop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbershop\_(film) "Barbershop (film)")_, _[Barbershop 2: Back in Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbershop\_2:\_Back\_in\_Business "Barbershop 2: Back in Business")_, _[Beauty Shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beauty\_Shop "Beauty Shop")_ and _[Barbershop: The Next Cut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbershop:\_The\_Next\_Cut "Barbershop: The Next Cut")_. He directed the 2009 biopic _[Notorious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notorious\_(2009\_film) "Notorious (2009 film)")_, about the late Brooklyn-born rapper [The Notorious B.I.G.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Notorious_B.I.G. "The Notorious B.I.G."),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-2) and directed and produced the drama [_The Hate U Give_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hate_U_Give_(film) "The Hate U Give (film)") (2018).

Tillman was nominated for the [Black Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Black_Film_Festival "American Black Film Festival") for Best Director for _Soul Food_ (1997). Tillman was also nominated for the [Black Reel Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Reel_Award "Black Reel Award") for Best Director and Best Screenplay for _Notorious_ (2009). In 2023, he won the [Children's and Family Emmy Award for Outstanding Young Teen Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_and_Family_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Young_Teen_Series "Children's and Family Emmy Award for Outstanding Young Teen Series") at the [2nd Children's and Family Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_Children's_and_Family_Emmy_Awards "2nd Children's and Family Emmy Awards") as executive producer on the [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+") sports drama series _[The Crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crossover\_(TV\_series) "The Crossover (TV series)")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-3)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=George_Tillman_Jr.&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Tillman was born in [Milwaukee, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee,_Wisconsin "Milwaukee, Wisconsin"). His father, George Tillman, worked at the [American Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Motors "American Motors") plant in [Kenosha, Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenosha,_Wisconsin "Kenosha, Wisconsin"), and his mother was a secretary.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-Alexander-4) Throughout his early childhood, Tillman would borrow his father's [8mm camera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8_mm_film "8 mm film") and would start to shoot things with Milwaukee's [Public-access television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public-access_television "Public-access television") cable TV channel.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-Alexander-4) By age eight, Tillman got his hands on his very first television script, _[All My Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All\_My\_Children "All My Children")_, and wrote his first soap opera as well as his first five-minute show. Tillman recalled, years later, to an interviewer in regard to receiving the _All My Children'_ s script," I told them about a certain plot change that I wanted and I thought I could help the characters out…That was the beginning for me, the writing."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-Alexander-4)

In 1975, Tillman became inspired to create his own films after seeing the film, _[Cooley High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooley\_High "Cooley High")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-Alexander-4) To Tillman, _Cooley High_ spoke to the African American audience in both tears and laughter, and Tillman decided he wanted to contribute to that medium, but did not necessarily know if he wanted to become an actor, writer or director. In 1973, when Tillman watched _[Five on the Black Hand Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five\_on\_the\_Black\_Hand\_Side "Five on the Black Hand Side")_ and _[Claudine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudine\_(film) "Claudine (film)")_ in 1974, he felt empowered and knew he wanted to become a filmmaker.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-Alexander-4) "Those were the films that made me realize that African American films- this is before they started calling some films of that era [Black exploitation films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blaxploitation "Blaxploitation")-spoke for us, and I wanted to be involved with that."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-Alexander-4)

Tillman went to [John Marshall High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Marshall_High_School_(Wisconsin) "John Marshall High School (Wisconsin)") in Milwaukee[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-5) and he took Mass Communications Magnet Classes. As a teenager, Tillman made amateur videos and created _Splice of Life_, which was a program for a local Public-access television.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-Gale-6) After high school, Tillman attended [Columbia College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_College_Chicago "Columbia College Chicago") in Chicago and majored in Film and Video. Tillman decided to move to Chicago because he thought a lot was happening there creatively. "There is a lot of theater there, and there are a lot of things happening in Chicago that I wanted to be a part of, so that's where I went to [film school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_school "Film school")," according to Tillman.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-Alexander-4) While in film school, he created a 30-minute short, _Paula_, which was a story of a 17-year-old, single African American mother who works in a [diner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diner "Diner") and motivates the people around her. _Paula'_ s success attributed to numerous awards including the Black Filmmaker's Hall of Fame Award "George Tillman Jr.".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Tillman_Jr#cite_note-7) and winning the Midwest Regional, Dramatic Category, of the

**Angela Thomas** (born September 20, 1988) is an American young adult author, known for her contributions to young adult fiction. She gained international recognition for her novel _[The Hate U Give](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hate\_U\_Give "The Hate U Give")_ (2017) which addresses police violence and racism. Her second young adult novel, _[On the Come Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On\_the\_Come\_Up "On the Come Up")_, was released on February 25, 2019. Her most recent novel, [Concrete Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concrete_Rose_(novel) "Concrete Rose (novel)"), was released on January 12, 2021.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angie_Thomas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Angie Thomas was born on September 20, 1988, in [Jackson, Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson,_Mississippi "Jackson, Mississippi"), where she was raised.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-2)

Thomas was subject to multiple instances of gun violence at a young age. She grew up near the home of assassinated civil rights activist, [Medgar Evers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medgar_Evers "Medgar Evers"), stating that her mother heard the gunshot that had killed him.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-philyaw-3) When she was 6 years old, Thomas witnessed a shootout between gangs.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-4)

In an interview with _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_, she recounted how her mother took her to the library the following day to show her that, "There was more to the world than what [Thomas] saw that day." This inspired her to take up writing.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-hirsch-5)

In her adolescence, Thomas shared her skills as a rapper, although her career in music was short-lived. She was, however, the subject of an article in _[Right On!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right\_On!\_(magazine) "Right On! (magazine)")_ magazine.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-keane-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-7) Thomas went on to obtain a [Bachelor of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Fine_Arts "Bachelor of Fine Arts")[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-bookaward-8) from [Belhaven University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belhaven_University "Belhaven University").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-mesure-9) She was the first Black teenager to graduate from her creative writing course.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-mesure-9)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angie_Thomas&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Thomas initially planned to write fantasy and middle grade novels, but began developing what would soon turn out to be her first novel while seeking publication for her earlier works. During her time in college, one of her professors suggested that her experiences were unique and that her writing could give a voice to those who had been silenced, thus developing _[The Hate U Give](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hate\_U\_Give "The Hate U Give")_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-10)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-philyaw-3) After its publication, _The Hate U Give_ was adapted into a [2018 film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hate_U_Give_(film) "The Hate U Give (film)") by [Fox 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox"), starring [Amandla Stenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amandla_Stenberg "Amandla Stenberg").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-mesure-9)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-keane-6)

The novel was influenced in part by contemporary events involving police violence, which includes the [shooting of Oscar Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_of_Oscar_Grant "Shooting of Oscar Grant"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-hirsch-5) as well as the deaths of [Trayvon Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trayvon_Martin "Trayvon Martin"), [Tamir Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_of_Tamir_Rice "Shooting of Tamir Rice"), [Michael Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_of_Michael_Brown "Shooting of Michael Brown"), and [Sandra Bland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Sandra_Bland "Death of Sandra Bland").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-hirsch-5)

Thomas cites [Tupac Shakur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupac_Shakur "Tupac Shakur") as inspiration for her writing. Especially in invoking a range of emotional responses from her readers. She has also stated that her writing is used to address and challenge social issues and stereotypes.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-npr-11)

## Activism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Angie_Thomas&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Activism")]

In an interview with _[Publishers Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publishers\_Weekly "Publishers Weekly")_, Thomas gives insight on her role as an activist: "I've always seen writing as a form of activism. If nothing else, books give us a glimpse into lives that we may not have known about before; they can promote empathy. There is the movement Black Lives Matter and the organization Black Lives Matter, and I respect what both are doing. I know [_The Hate U Give_] is an 'issue' book, but I didn't necessarily want it to be that way... I wanted to make something that is so political seem personal. While I wanted Khalil to represent these young men who lose their lives and are quickly labeled thugs, I wanted [the plot of the book] to be its own thing. I didn't want to disrespect anyone's family, anyone's memory."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angie_Thomas#cite_note-12)

**Greta Celeste Gerwig** ([/ˈ ɡ ɜːr w ɪ ɡ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_GUR-wig_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig#cite_note-1) born August 4, 1983) is an American actress and filmmaker. She was initially known for working on various [mumblecore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumblecore "Mumblecore") films, such as _[Baghead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baghead "Baghead")_ (2008) and _[Yeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeast\_(film) "Yeast (film)")_ (2008), in which she became an important figure in the movement.[[2]](

The **44th [Telluride Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telluride_Film_Festival "Telluride Film Festival")** was held on September 1–4, 2017, in [Telluride, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telluride,_Colorado "Telluride, Colorado"), United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/44th_Telluride_Film_Festival#cite_note-1)

Director [Joshua Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshua_Oppenheimer "Joshua Oppenheimer") was appointed as the guest director of the event.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/44th_Telluride_Film_Festival#cite_note-2) Telluride honored [Edward Lachman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Lachman "Edward Lachman") and [Christian Bale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Bale "Christian Bale") as the [Silver Medallion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telluride_Film_Festival_Silver_Medallion "Telluride Film Festival Silver Medallion") winners.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/44th_Telluride_Film_Festival#cite_note-3) The Special Medallion was awarded to Katriel Schory of Israeli Film Fund.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/44th_Telluride_Film_Festival#cite_note-4)

**A24 Films LLC**, commonly referred to as **A24**, is an American [independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_film "Independent film") entertainment company specializing in [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film "Film") and [television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television "Television") production, as well as [film distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_distribution "Film distribution"). They distribute and produce [arthouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_film "Art film") films, many of which have gone on to develop cult followings. **The ReFrame Stamp for Gender-Balanced Production** certification is awarded by [ReFrame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ReFrame "ReFrame") to corporations and media that show progress toward [gender equality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_equality "Gender equality") and greater representation of women in key roles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-2)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 5: [icon]](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg/20px-Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wiki_letter_w_cropped.svg)This section **needs expansion**. You can help by [adding missing information](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=). _(March 2019)_

On June 8, 2018, the ReFrame Stamp program was launched to promote and recognize gender-balanced productions in film and television based on data from [IMDb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMDb "IMDb")Pro on how many women are involved in a production in front of and behind the camera.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-3) On September 26, the Stamp program expanded to include submissions for TV shows and movies from cable and streaming platforms.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-4) ReFrame entered into a partnership in February 2020 with Delta Air Lines in which two in-flight channels dedicated to films and television programs respectively with the ReFrame Stamp would be featured.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-5) The ReFrame Movie Channel launched with 29 initial offerings including [_Wonder Woman_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_Woman_(2017_film) "Wonder Woman (2017 film)"), [_The Hate U Give_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hate_U_Give_(film) "The Hate U Give (film)"), _[Ocean's 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean's\_8 "Ocean's 8")_, and [_Lady Bird_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Bird_(film) "Lady Bird (film)"). The ReFrame Show Channel's initial releases included [_Supergirl_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergirl_(TV_series) "Supergirl (TV series)"), [_Empire_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_(2015_TV_series) "Empire (2015 TV series)"), [_How to Get Away With Murder_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_to_Get_Away_with_Murder "How to Get Away with Murder"), and [_Better Things_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Better_Things_(TV_series) "Better Things (TV series)"). These offerings were planned to cycle on a monthly basis with additions in each lineup.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-6)

## Submission process

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Submission process")]

Qualifying films must be distributed either theatrically or via streaming, while TV shows are counted in relation to the calendar for the [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award"). Films and television which are not considered top 100 grossing projects may be considered through a rolling open call via a manual submission process.

During any given submission period, the individual entering the information regarding the feature film which has been distributed theatrically or via streaming must utilize the Narrative Feature, Animated Feature, or Television submission form. As of 2019, information provided in each submission must include the project title, year of release, studio (or platform), distributor, and contact information for both a production and studio/distributor representative. The submission must specify the positions of each woman involved in qualifying areas for consideration, as well as whether each of those specified is a [person of color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Person_of_color "Person of color").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-8) Appeals for ReFrame Stamp submissions are reviewed using an independent panel and may be submitted via email.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-9)

## Criteria

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Criteria")]

Based on a points system, [narrative films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narrative_film "Narrative film") and animated films[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-FilmStampCriteria-10) and TV programs[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-11) must achieve four points within the eight defined qualifying categories with at least two points in the categories of female director, writer, and lead. Double points are awarded for women of color in important positions. Screen time analysis is done with the [Geena Davis Inclusion Quotient (GD-IQ)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geena_Davis_Institute_on_Gender_in_Media "Geena Davis Institute on Gender in Media")[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_],[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-12) while points are calculated by an algorithm and given to the films or TV programs that meet the requirements. After the stamp is awarded, a logo is added to the end credits.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ReFrame_Stamp#cite_note-:02-13) The criteria are subject to change accordingly with the evolving industry.

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Film")]

*   Female lead (Top 1 slot listed on the call sheet) 
    *   1 point for a female lead
    *   2 points for a female lead of color

*   Female co-lead (Top 2-5 slots on the call sheet) 
    *   1 point for a female lead
    *   2 points for a female lead of color

*   Female representation on screen 
    *   1 point when 50% of the screen time is female
    *   2 points when 25% of the screen time is females of color

*   Female director 
    *   1 point for a female director
    *   2 points for a female director of color

*   Female writer 
    *   1 point for a credited female writer
    *   2 points for a credited female writer of color

*   Female producer 
    *   1 point for a female producer
    *   2 points for a female producer of color

*   50% of department heads are female 
    *   1 point for 50% female department heads
    *   2 points for 25% female department heads of color

*   50% of crew members 
    *   1 point for 50% female crew
    *   2 points for 25% female crew of color

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_ReFrame_Stamp&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Television")]

*   Female lead (Top 1 slot listed on the call sheet) 
    *   1 point for a female lead
    *   2 points for a female lead of color

*   Female season regulars (Top 2-5 slots on the call sheet) 
    *   1 point if 50% of season regulars are female
    *   2 points if 25% of season regulars are females of color

*   Female showrunner 
    *   1 point for a female showrunner
    *   2 points for a female showrunner of color

*   Female writing staff 
    *   1 point if 50% of writing staff are female writers (per season)
    *   2 points if 25% of writing staff are female writers of color (per season)

*   Female producer 
    *   1 point for at least one female non-writing producer
    *   2 points for at least one female non-writing producer of color

*   Female director 
    *   1 point for 50% of episodes directed by female directors (per season)
    *   2 points for 25% of episodes directed by female directors of color (per season)

*   Designated female production personnel 
    *   1 point if 50% of the designated production personnel are female
    *   2 points if 25% of the designated production personnel are female of color

*   Female crew 
    *   1 point for 50% female crew
    *   2 points for 25% female crew of color

Organizers of the annual [ReFrame](link_54) Report said Wednesday that 29 of the 100 most popular films of 2022 met the criteria to be awarded a [ReFrame Stamp](link_55) for gender-balanced productions, a list that includes Oscar Best Picture nominees like Sarah Polley’s _Women Talking_ and The Daniels’ _[Everything Everywhere All at Once](link_56)_, as well as Gina Prince-Bythewood’s _[The Woman King](link_57)_ and Disney/Marvel’s _[Black Panther: Wakanda Forever](link_58)_.

![Image 5](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/ReFrame-Stamp.png?w=300)

The ReFrame initiative, launched in 2017 by Sundance Institute, Women in Film and IMDbPro, aims to identify and reward features that hire women or other underrepresented individuals on at least 50% of key roles including writer, director, producer, lead, co-leads and department heads. More points are awarded to productions that hire women of color in key positions, and to those with overall gender parity among their crews.

### Related Stories

The report found that hiring levels for women in the top 100 productions (as determined by IMDb page views) continued on a flat trajectory in 2022 after seeing 66% growth from 2017 to 2018, and 35% growth from 2018 to 2019. There with no significant gains for women in key roles including directors (14%) and writers (31%) among the top 100 films in 2022, while the number of women of color hired as directors (2%) and writers (2%) both dropped year-over-year.

No non-binary or gender non-conforming people were hired as writers or directors among the top 100 films last year.

Among studios in 2022, Sony had the highest stamp rate, with 50% of their six listed releases earning the nod, followed by A24, with a 40% stamp rate. Netflix had the most entries on the top 100 list with 28 films; 11 of those earned the stamp (39% of entries).

The report found that 40.4% of films released directly to streaming services earned the stamp, while only 21.8% of films with a traditional theatrical release made the cut.

“We celebrate these new ReFrame Stamp recipients, the filmmaking teams who demonstrated a commitment to equitable hiring, and the successes of these films, which serve as a reminder that feature films can be critically well-received, beloved by audiences,_and_ created with a commitment to inclusion,” ReFrame director Andria Wilson Mirza said Wednesday. “Our frustration lies with the stagnancy of these numbers. No more than 29% of the Top 100 films in any given year since ReFrame and IMDbPro began tracking this data in 2017 have earned the Stamp, meaning that the majority of popular titles did not meet baseline criteria for gender-balanced hiring.”

# 2022 ReFrame Film Stamp Recipients

The ReFrame Stamp is awarded to features that hire women or individuals of other underrepresented gender identities/expressions (including those who are non-binary or gender non-conforming) in at least 50% of key roles. Additional points are awarded to productions that hire women of color in key positions, and to those with overall gender parity in their crews. ReFrame determines which productions met Stamp criteria based on an extensive analysis of data provided by IMDbPro, including a list of the 100 most popular films of 2022 and the Box Office Mojo list of the top 100 domestic grossing films of 2022. Films that applied for the ReFrame Stamp and Stamped Academy Award nominated films are also included in the list.

Ryan Kyle Coogler is an American film-maker and producer from Oakland, California. Highly critically acclaimed, he has directed the films [Fruitvale Station (2013)](link_52), [Creed (2015)](link_53), [Black Panther (2018)](link_54), [Black Panther: Wakanda Forever (2022)](link_55) and [Sinners (2025)](link_56), all of which he also wrote, and all of which feature [Michael B. Jordan](link_57). His first film was an independent success, and the rest have been major blockbusters, with Black Panther becoming one of the most widely seen superhero movies ever, and Sinners one of the highest-grossing horror films ever made. He has also produced the Creed sequels, as well as Judas and the Black Messiah and Space Jam: A New Legacy. He has been married to Zinzi Evans, with whom he has two children, since 2016.

Actress and activist Olivia Wilde is a modern day renaissance woman, starring in many acclaimed film productions, while simultaneously giving back to the community.  
  
She was born on March 10, 1984 in New York City. Her parents are [Leslie Cockburn](link_52) (née Leslie Corkill Redlich) and [Andrew Cockburn](link_53). Her mother is American-born and her father was born in London, England to an upper-class British family; he also later became a citizen of Ireland. Wilde is the middle child, having an older sister, Chloe Cockburn, and, a younger brother, Charlie Cockburn. She is of English, Irish, Scottish, German, and Manx descent.  
  
She was raised in Georgetown, Washington, D.C., and spent her summers in Ardmore, County Waterford, Ireland. She attended the private Georgetown Day School, as well as, Phillips Academy in Andover, Massachusetts, graduating in 2002. She was accepted to Bard College, another highly selective private school in Duchess County, New York but deferred her enrollment three times in order to pursue an acting career. She later studied at the Gaiety School of Acting in Dublin, Ireland.  
  
Wilde is known for her television roles as Alex Kelly in [The O.C. (2003)](link_54) from 2004-2005 and Dr. Remy "Thirteen" Hadley in the medical-drama television series, [House (2004)](link_55) when she joined the cast in 2007 and appeared on the show until the series end in 2012.  
  
Wilde is a board member of the organization "Artists for Peace and Justice," which supports communities in Haiti through programs in education, health care, and dignity through the performing arts. She has served as executive producer on several documentary short films, including, [Sun City Picture House (2010)](link_56), which is about a community in Haiti that rallies to build a movie theater after the disastrous 2010 earthquake and [Baseball in the Time of Cholera (2012)](link_57), which explored the cholera epidemic in Haiti.  
  
Wilde is known for her roles in [Year One (2009)](link_58), [Tron: Legacy (2010)](link_59), [Cowboys & Aliens (2011)](link_60), [In Time (2011)](link_61), [People Like Us (2012)](link_62), [Her (2013)](link_63), [Rush (2013)](link_64), [Drinking Buddies (2013)](link_65), [The Longest Week (2014)](link_66), [Love the Coopers (2015)](link_67), and [Meadowland (2015)](link_68).  
  
Since 2011, Wilde had been in a relationship with [Jason Sudeikis](link_69). They have two children together, Otis Alexander Sudeikis (born April 20, 2014) and Daisy Josephine Sudeikis (born October 11, 2016). In November 2020, they announced that they had ended their relationship.  
  
Wilde made her Broadway debut in the play "1984" at the Hudson Theatre in New York City in 2017. She has recently starred in [Life Itself (2018)](link_70) and [A Vigilante (2018)](link_71).

# ‘The Woman King’, ‘Everything Everywhere All At Once’, ‘Black Panther: Wakanda Forever’, ‘Women Talking’ Among ReFrame Stamp Recipients

![Image 1](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Patrick-Hipes-2.jpg?w=193&h=193&crop=1)

By [Patrick Hipes](https://deadline.com/author/phipes/)

## [Patrick Hipes](https://deadline.com/author/phipes/)

Executive Managing Editor

#### More Stories By Patrick

*   [American Cinematheque Award Skipping 2026 After Sked Conflict With Honoree Ryan Gosling](https://deadline.com/2026/10/american-cinematheque-award-skips-2026-ryan-gosling-1237145690/)
*   [Tony Romo And CBS Sports Part Ways After His Drunk-Driving Arrest](https://deadline.com/2026/10/tony-romo-out-cbs-sports-1237145506/)
*   [‘Ink’ Helmer Danny Boyle To Receive Gotham Film Awards’ Director Tribute](https://deadline.com/2026/09/danny-boyle-gotham-film-awards-director-tribute-1237127742/)

[View All](https://deadline.com/author/phipes/)

March 1, 2023 4:27pm

![Image 2: The Woman King](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/The-Woman-King.jpg?crop=524px%2C0px%2C2233px%2C1251px&resize=681%2C383)

(L-R) Lashana Lynch, Viola Davis and Sheila Atim in 'The Woman King'TriStar Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection

Organizers of the annual ReFrame Report said Wednesday that 29 of the 100 most popular films of 2022 met the criteria to be awarded a ReFrame Stamp for gender-balanced productions, a list that includes Oscar Best Picture nominees like Sarah Polley’s _Women Talking_ and The Daniels’ _Everything Everywhere All at Once_, as well as Gina Prince-Bythewood’s _The Woman King_ and Disney/Marvel’s _Black Panther: Wakanda Forever_.

![Image 3](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/ReFrame-Stamp.png?w=300)

The ReFrame initiative, launched in 2017 by Sundance Institute, Women in Film and IMDbPro, aims to identify and reward features that hire women or other underrepresented individuals on at least 50% of key roles including writer, director, producer, lead, co-leads and department heads. More points are awarded to productions that hire women of color in key positions, and to those with overall gender parity among their crews.

The report found that hiring levels for women in the top 100 productions (as determined by IMDb page views) continued on a flat trajectory in 2022 after seeing 66% growth from 2017 to 2018, and 35% growth from 2018 to 2019. There with no significant gains for women in key roles including directors (14%) and writers (31%) among the top 100 films in 2022, while the number of women of color hired as directors (2%) and writers (2%) both dropped year-over-year.

No non-binary or gender non-conforming people were hired as writers or directors among the top 100 films last year.

Among studios in 2022, Sony had the highest stamp rate, with 50% of their six listed releases earning the nod, followed by A24, with a 40% stamp rate. Netflix had the most entries on the top 100 list with 28 films; 11 of those earned the stamp (39% of entries).

The report found that 40.4% of films released directly to streaming services earned the stamp, while only 21.8% of films with a traditional theatrical release made the cut.

“We celebrate these new ReFrame Stamp recipients, the filmmaking teams who demonstrated a commitment to equitable hiring, and the successes of these films, which serve as a reminder that feature films can be critically well-received, beloved by audiences,_and_ created with a commitment to inclusion,” ReFrame director Andria Wilson Mirza said Wednesday. “Our frustration lies with the stagnancy of these numbers. No more than 29% of the Top 100 films in any given year since ReFrame and IMDbPro began tracking this data in 2017 have earned the Stamp, meaning that the majority of popular titles did not meet baseline criteria for gender-balanced hiring.”

Read the full report and see the full list of 2022 stamp recipients [here](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/ReFrame-Report-2022.pdf).

The ReFrame coalition has awarded 26 feature films released in 2019 with its [ReFrame Stamp](https://deadline.com/tag/reframe-stamp/), which recognizes the top 100-grossing gender-balanced narrative and animated features. The list, which grew from 20 total films that earned the stamp a year ago, includes _[Booksmart](https://deadline.com/tag/booksmart/), Captain Marvel, Harriet, Hustlers_ and Oscar Best Picture nominee _Little Women_.

This reflects gains for women in the important roles of director, department heads, and women of color leads and co-leads. With an aim to increase the number of women of all backgrounds working in film, TV, and media, the ReFrame Stamp, which is showcased in end credits and appears on IMDb, serves as a mark of distinction for projects that have demonstrated success in gender-balanced hiring. Additional points are awarded to content that has women of color in key positions.

“We launched the ReFrame Stamp with IMDbPro three years ago as a change lever to promote more inclusive hiring practices at all levels of production,” said ReFrame director Alison Emilio. “The call to action is simple. Use the ReFrame criteria, improve hiring outcomes, get the stamp.”

“I see the ReFrame Stamp as an important lever for change to help women and people of color break through the boundaries and level the playing field,” said _Booksmart_ director Olivia Wilde. “Stamp criteria helped me focus on who would be best for the job – and I was able to hire an incredibly diverse and balanced crew to curate the environment I always wanted to see on a set.”
