**Mick Garris** (born December 4, 1951) is an American [filmmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmmaker "Filmmaker"), [screenwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenwriter "Screenwriter") and [novelist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novelist "Novelist") born in [Santa Monica, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Monica,_California "Santa Monica, California"). He is best known for his work in the horror film genre, as well as making [Stephen King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King "Stephen King") adaptations.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-1)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mick_Garris&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Garris was born in [Santa Monica, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Monica,_California "Santa Monica, California") and raised in [Van Nuys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Nuys "Van Nuys").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mick_Garris&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

He is known for his work in the horror genre. He has worked with [Stephen King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King "Stephen King") several times, such as directing the [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film")_[Sleepwalkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleepwalkers\_(1992\_film) "Sleepwalkers (1992 film)")_, written by King and starring [Mädchen Amick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A4dchen_Amick "Mädchen Amick")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-2) and is the creator of the [Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showtime_(TV_network) "Showtime (TV network)") series _[Masters of Horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters\_of\_Horror "Masters of Horror")_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-3) and the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") series _[Fear Itself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear\_Itself\_(TV\_series) "Fear Itself (TV series)")_. Garris won a 1986 [Edgar Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Award "Edgar Award") for an episode he wrote for the [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg")-produced television series _[Amazing Stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazing\_Stories\_(1985\_TV\_series) "Amazing Stories (1985 TV series)")_. Garris directed the [FEARnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FEARnet "FEARnet")[web series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_series "Web series")_Post Mortem_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-4) He contributes to the web series [Trailers From Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trailers_From_Hell "Trailers From Hell"). Garris was also the co-screenwriter and executive producer of _[Hocus Pocus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hocus\_Pocus\_(1993\_film) "Hocus Pocus (1993 film)")_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-5) Garris directed the 2011 miniseries adaption of [Stephen King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King "Stephen King")'s novel _[Bag of Bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bag\_of\_Bones "Bag of Bones")_[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-6) and the documentary film _Pure in Heart: The Life and Legacy of Lon Chaney Jr._, about the life and work of Legend actor [Lon Chaney Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lon_Chaney_Jr. "Lon Chaney Jr."),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-7) which screened on the Horror-Rama 2015 in October 2015.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-8) He has a role, as Himself in the biography horror film _[Digging Up the Marrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digging\_Up\_the\_Marrow "Digging Up the Marrow")_, from indie director [Adam Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Green_(filmmaker) "Adam Green (filmmaker)").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-9)

As of 2015, he is also a member of the board of advisers for the Hollywood Horror Museum.

On January 16, 2018, it was announced that Mick Garris's horror podcast _Post Mortem_ would be joining [Blumhouse's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blumhouse_Productions "Blumhouse Productions") podcast network.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Garris#cite_note-10)

## Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mick_Garris&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Awards")]

*   Garris received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2006 [New York City Horror Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Horror_Film_Festival "New York City Horror Film Festival"). He received the award in person after a screening of his _[Masters of Horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters\_of\_Horror "Masters of Horror")_ episode "[Valerie on the Stairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valerie_on_the_Stairs "Valerie on the Stairs")".

**David Maxwell Kirschner** (born May 29, 1955) is an American film and television producer and screenwriter. His producing credits include [Don Bluth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Bluth "Don Bluth")'s _[An American Tail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_American\_Tail "An American Tail")_ (also wrote) and _[Titan A.E.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titan\_A.E. "Titan A.E.")_ animated features as well as _[Cats Don't Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cats\_Don't\_Dance "Cats Don't Dance")_, _[Curious George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curious\_George\_(film) "Curious George (film)")_, the _[Child's Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child's\_Play\_(franchise) "Child's Play (franchise)")_ horror franchise.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=David_Kirschner&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

After studying at the [University of Southern California School of Cinematic Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Southern_California_School_of_Cinematic_Arts "University of Southern California School of Cinematic Arts"), Kirschner began his career designing album cover art for [Neil Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Diamond "Neil Diamond"), including _[The Jazz Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jazz\_Singer\_(soundtrack) "The Jazz Singer (soundtrack)")_, and illustrating characters for the _[Muppets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muppets "Muppets")_ and _[Sesame Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesame\_Street "Sesame Street")_. In 1983, Kirschner created and released children's book series _[Rose Petal Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose\_Petal\_Place "Rose Petal Place")_, which spawned two Television specials, toys, clothing, and a wide array of licensed consumer products. In 1986, Kirschner created and executive produced _[An American Tail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_American\_Tail "An American Tail")_, which was co-executive produced by [Steven Spielberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg"), and, at its release, was the highest-grossing non-Disney produced animated feature of all time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-1) It was followed by its theatrical sequel _[An American Tail: Fievel Goes West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_American\_Tail:\_Fievel\_Goes\_West "An American Tail: Fievel Goes West")_ (1991), the television series _[Fievel's American Tails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fievel's\_American\_Tails "Fievel's American Tails")_, and two direct-to-video sequels. In 1986, David Kirschner signed a deal with [United Artists Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Artists "United Artists") and [MGM/UA Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGM_Television "MGM Television") for development, production and distribution of major motion picture and television projects for a two-year deal.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-2) Kirschner was appointed chairman of [Hanna-Barbera Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanna-Barbera_Productions "Hanna-Barbera Productions") in 1989,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-5) where he wrote / created and executive produced many films, specials and shows, including _[Wake, Rattle & Roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake,\_Rattle\_&\_Roll "Wake, Rattle & Roll")_, _[Gravedale High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gravedale\_High "Gravedale High")_ and _[The Pirates of Dark Water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pirates\_of\_Dark\_Water "The Pirates of Dark Water")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-6)

Kirschner also designed the [Chucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chucky_(Child's_Play) "Chucky (Child's Play)")[animatronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animatronic "Animatronic") doll which is featured in the _[Child's Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child's\_Play\_(franchise) "Child's Play (franchise)")_ series.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-7) He has produced all seven films in the original franchise,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-8) as well as executive producing the [_Chucky_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chucky_(TV_series) "Chucky (TV series)") television series.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-11) Other notable productions include 1997's _[Cats Don't Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cats\_Don't\_Dance "Cats Don't Dance")_,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-14) winner of the 25th annual [Annie Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Awards "Annie Awards") for Best Animated Feature,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Kirschner#cite_note-15) 2006's _[Curious George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curious\_George\_(film) "Curious George (film)")_, based upon the [book series of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curious_George "Curious George"), _[Martian Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martian\_Child "Martian Child")_, and Golden Globe-nominated _[Miss Potter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss\_Potter "Miss Potter")_. His 2010s/2020s work includes executive producer on _[Curious George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curious\_George\_(TV\_series) "Curious George (TV series)")_, _[Hocus Pocus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hocus\_Pocus\_2 "Hocus Pocus 2")_ ([Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+")), _Random_ (In Pre-Production for [The Weinstein Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weinstein_Company "The Weinstein Company")) and _Garden District_ (In-Development for [Dimension Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimension_Films "Dimension Films")). Kirschner is currently head of his own production company, David Kirschner Productions.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

American film director

| Adam Shankman |

| [![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Adam-shankman.jpg/250px-Adam-shankman.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adam-shankman.jpg) Adam Shankman in 2007 |
| Born | Adam Michael Shankman (1964-11-27) November 27, 1964 (age 61) [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), U.S. |

| Years active | 1983–present |

**Adam Michael Shankman** (born November 27, 1964)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-tvguidebio-1) is an American film director, producer, writer, dancer, author, actor, and choreographer. He was a permanent judge on seasons 6–7 of the television program _[So You Think You Can Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So\_You\_Think\_You\_Can\_Dance\_(American\_TV\_series) "So You Think You Can Dance (American TV series)")_. He began his professional career in [musical theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theater "Musical theater") and was a dancer in music videos for [Paula Abdul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Abdul "Paula Abdul") and [Janet Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Jackson "Janet Jackson"). Shankman has choreographed dozens of films and directed several feature-length films, including _[A Walk to Remember](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Walk\_to\_Remember "A Walk to Remember")_, _[Bringing Down the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bringing\_Down\_the\_House\_(film) "Bringing Down the House (film)")_, _[The Pacifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pacifier "The Pacifier")_, and the musicals _[Hairspray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hairspray\_(2007\_film) "Hairspray (2007 film)"), [Rock of Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock\_of\_Ages\_(2012\_film) "Rock of Ages (2012 film)")_ and _[Disenchanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disenchanted\_(film) "Disenchanted (film)")_.

His company, [Offspring Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offspring_Entertainment "Offspring Entertainment") (which he co-owns with his sister), produces films and television for various studios and networks.

Shankman is also currently co-writing young adult novels for [Simon & Schuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_&_Schuster "Simon & Schuster") imprint [Atheneum Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atheneum_Books "Atheneum Books") for Young Readers. The books, co-written with author Laura Lee Sullivan, follow the story of [rags to riches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rags_to_riches "Rags to riches") Lucille O'Malley as she becomes Hollywood's "it girl", navigating a murder mystery and meeting her match, Frederick van der Waals.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adam_Shankman&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Shankman was born in Los Angeles[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-3) to an upper-middle-class [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") family.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-4) He is the son of Phyllis (née Perper), a licensed practitioner in [Gestalt therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gestalt_therapy "Gestalt therapy"), and Ned Shankman, an entertainment lawyer and manager for such acts as [Barry White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_White "Barry White"), the American band [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_(American_band) "X (American band)"), and [Sister Sledge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_Sledge "Sister Sledge").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-5) His sister, Jennifer Shankman-Gibgot, was born when Shankman was four years old. He attended Palisades High School before attending [Juilliard School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juilliard_School "Juilliard School").

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adam_Shankman&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Adam_Shankman&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

After graduating from Palisades,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-6) Shankman was a performing intern and junior company member of the prestigious [Children's Theatre Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_Theatre_Company "Children's Theatre Company") in Minneapolis. Having been accepted for both dancing and acting at Juilliard, he chose dance as his major without having any previous formal training.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-white-7) He dropped out of college to dance in musical theater and at nineteen he was cast in his first professional show, _West Side Story_, at the esteemed [Michigan Opera Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_Opera_Theater "Michigan Opera Theater").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-8)

Shankman moved back to Los Angeles and started dancing in music videos. He was a dancer in Janet Jackson's "Alright" video,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-white-7) as well as in an [MC Skat Kat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MC_Skat_Kat "MC Skat Kat") video with Paula Abdul.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman#cite_note-9) Shankman broke into professional choreography in a 1989 music video for rapper MC Shan with director [Julien Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Temple "Julien Temple"). When the hired choreographer fell through, Shankman lied and said that he had done choreography for Janet Jackson and Paula Abdul. ## ReFrame and IMDbPro Announce 2022 ReFrame Stamp Film Recipients

Published

Mar 1, 2023 11:46am EST

linkedin facebook x email reddit

**29 of the 100 Most Popular Films of 2022 Meet ReFrame Criteria for Gender-Balanced Production including Everything Everywhere All At Once, The Woman King, and Black Panther: Wakanda Forever**

**Report reveals entertainment production hiring levels for women have flatlined in the last four years, following a 125% jump between 2017-2019**

LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- [ReFrame](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.reframeproject.org%2Fabout-1&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=ReFrame&index=1&md5=4ab6d396a03493f84bf905d05aaa543b), the collaborative initiative launched in 2017 by Sundance Institute and WIF to advance gender equity in the screen industries, and [IMDbPro](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.imdbpro.com%2F&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=IMDbPro&index=2&md5=f9756b00e77dc5bd55b3544b0ae9cadb), the essential resource for entertainment industry professionals, today announced the findings of its most recent ReFrame Report, which shows that 29 of the 100 most popular films of 2022 meet ReFrame Stamp criteria for gender-balanced production. The ReFrame Report can be viewed [HERE](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.reframeproject.org%2Fstamp&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=HERE&index=3&md5=eb880175eae029f55480b71d1a2efc55). Recipients include some of 2022’s most critically acclaimed films from women directors, Gina Prince-Bythewood’s The Woman King and Sarah Polley’s Women Talking, and also films from male directors including Ryan Coogler’s Black Panther: Wakanda Forever and The Daniels’ Everything Everywhere All At Once, also the year’s leader in Academy Award nominations.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: [https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20230228006509/en/](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20230228006509/en/)

The ReFrame Stamp is awarded to features that hire women or individuals of other underrepresented gender identities/expressions (including those who are non-binary or gender non-conforming) in at least 50% of key roles including writer, director, producer, lead, co-leads, and department heads (Cinematographer, Production Designer, Casting Director, Costume Designer, Editor, Composer, Music Supervisor, VFX Supervisor). Additional points are awarded to productions that hire women of color in key positions, and to those with overall gender parity in their crews. View full criteria [here](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.reframeproject.org%2Fstamp-criteria-film&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=here&index=4&md5=50a8fa07703d58ae7a278c5e4eff8c24).

The report additionally reveals that despite significant growth in gender-equitable hiring among the 100 most popular films in 2018 (66% increase over 2017) and 2019 (35% increase over 2018), entertainment production hiring levels for women have plateaued over the last four years, with no significant advancement for women in key roles between 2019 and 2022.

**Key findings of the ReFrame Report when compared with 2021 results:**

*    There was no increase in the number of women directors hired across the Top 100 feature films (14% in 2022 and 2021), and a decrease in the number of women of color hired as directors (2% in 2022 vs. 4% in 2021) 
*    There was no significant increase in the number of women writers hired across the Top 100 feature films (32% in 2022 vs. 31% in 2021), and a decrease in the number of women of color hired as writers (2% in 2022 vs. 9% in 2021) 
*    No non-binary or gender non-conforming people were hired as writers or directors across the Top 100 feature films (0% in 2022 and 2021) 
*    No increase in the number of Academy Award nominees for Best Picture which qualify for the Stamp (30% in 2022 and 2021) 

**Additional Findings:**

**Production Budgets:** The production budgets of eligible films were also reviewed. The highest percentage of Stamped films came in at the budget level of $15-25 million, with 42% of films at this level earning the Stamp. While 17% of films at the highest budget level ($100 million or more) earned the Stamp, only one of those was directed by a woman, Domee Shi’s Turning Red, which was released exclusively to the Disney+ streaming service.

**Studio Rankings:**The IMDbPro 100 most popular films of 2022 includes productions from all major studios. In a studio-by-studio analysis, Sony had the highest Stamp success rate, with 50% of their 6 listed releases earning the Stamp, followed by A24, with a 40% Stamp rate. Netflix had the most entries on the top 100 list with 28 films, and 11 of those earned the Stamp (39% of entries). Disney and its subsidiaries followed; of their 21 releases that made the top 100 List, 8 earned the Stamp (38% of entries). 40.4% of films released directly to streaming services earned the Stamp, while only 21.8% of films with a traditional theatrical release qualified.

“We celebrate these new ReFrame Stamp recipients, the filmmaking teams who demonstrated a commitment to equitable hiring, and the successes of these films, which serve as a reminder that feature films can be critically well-received, beloved by audiences, and created with a commitment to inclusion,” said Andria Wilson Mirza, ReFrame’s Director. “Our frustration lies with the stagnancy of these numbers. No more than 29% of the Top 100 films in any given year since ReFrame and IMDbPro began tracking this data in 2017 have earned the Stamp, meaning that the majority of popular titles did not meet baseline criteria for gender-balanced hiring.”

ReFrame encourages all fiction feature films released in North America to implement equitable hiring practices and [earn the ReFrame Stamp](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.reframeproject.org%2Fstamp&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=earn+the+ReFrame+Stamp&index=5&md5=3bd50c29d7c83fc794682d86e98ada68). Outside of the 29 films in the Top 100 receiving the ReFrame Stamp, more than 50 additional films released in 2022 also met Stamp criteria, including She Said (Universal, Dir. Maria Schrader), Aftersun (A24, Dir. Charlotte Wells), Till (United Artists, Dir. Chinonye Chukwu), and Marcel the Shell With Shoes On (A24, Dir. Dean Fleischer-Camp). A list of all 2022 Stamped films is available on ReFrame’s [website](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.reframeproject.org%2F&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=website&index=6&md5=37fa6504e839ccedade68400823cf863) and at [IMDb.com/ReFrame](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.imdb.com%2Freframe%2F&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=IMDb.com%2FReFrame&index=7&md5=b90f6868b665f3401ca14c1288dbaa53).

ReFrame determines which productions met Stamp criteria based on an extensive analysis of data provided by IMDbPro, including a list of the 100 most popular films of 2022 (based on the actual page views of the more than 200 million monthly visitors to IMDb worldwide, including both theatrical and streaming releases). ReFrame reviewed additional data provided by IMDb, including the Box Office Mojo list of the top 100 domestic-grossing films of 2022, and the results remained consistent with 27 of those 100 films qualifying for the Stamp.

**About ReFrame**

Founded and led by Sundance Institute and Women In Film, Los Angeles (WIF), ReFrame is an initiative that employs a unique strategy: a peer-to-peer approach, in which ReFrame Ambassadors engage with senior industry decision-makers at over 50 Partner Companies to implement ReFrame systemic change programs. The initiative’s goals are to provide research, support, and a practical framework that can be used by Partner companies to mitigate bias during the creative decision-making and hiring process, celebrate successes, and measure progress toward a more gender-representative industry on all levels.

The ReFrame Council, which leads the strategic direction of the organization with ReFrame Director Andria Wilson Mirza, includes the initiative’s founding members, WIF Executive Director Kirsten Schaffer, former Sundance CEO Keri Putnam, and Oscar-winning producer, WIF President Emeritas and founder of Welle Entertainment Cathy Schulman, alongside Channing Dungey (Chairman, Warner Bros. Television Group), Franklin Leonard (Founder, The Black List), Rena Ronson (Head of UTA Independent Film Group), and Michelle Satter (Founding Senior Director, Artist Programs, Sundance Institute). ReFrame is made possible by support from The David and Lura Lovell Foundation; IMDbPro; Netflix’s Fund for Creative Equity; Endeavor Impact; Delta Air Lines; Adobe; and the Women at Sundance Leadership Council.

**About Sundance Institute**

As a champion and curator of independent stories, the Sundance Institute provides and preserves the space for artists across storytelling media to create and thrive. Founded in 1981 by Robert Redford, the Institute's signature Labs, granting, and mentorship programs, dedicated to developing new work, take place throughout the year in the U.S. and internationally. [Sundance Collab](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fcollab.sundance.org%2F&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=Sundance+Collab&index=106&md5=210cf98094343d237701780b60837602), a digital community platform, brings a global cohort of working artists together to learn from each other and Sundance Advisors and connect in a creative space, developing and sharing works in progress. The Sundance Film Festival and other public programs connect audiences and artists to ignite new ideas, discover original voices, and build a community dedicated to independent storytelling. Sundance Institute has supported and showcased such projects as Summer of Soul (...or, When the Revolution Could Not Be Televised), CODA, Flee, Passing, Clemency, Never Rarely Sometimes Always, Zola, On the Record, Boys State, The Farewell, Honeyland, One Child Nation, The Souvenir, The Infiltrators, Sorry to Bother You, Won't You Be My Neighbor?, Hereditary, Call Me By Your Name, Get Out, The Big Sick, Mudbound, Fruitvale Station, City So Real, Top of the Lake, Between the World & Me, Wild Goose Dreams and Fun Home. **About WIF**

Founded in 1973 as Women In Film, Los Angeles, WIF advocates for and advances the careers of women working in the screen industries, to achieve parity and transform culture. We support women and people of marginalized genders in front of and behind the camera and across all levels of experience. We work to change culture through our distinguished pipeline programs; we advocate for gender parity through research, education, and media campaigns; and we build a community centered around these goals. Membership is open to all screen industry professionals, and more information can be found on our website: [wif.org](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwomeninfilm.org%2F&esheet=53354092&newsitemid=20230228006509&lan=en-US&anchor=wif.org&index=112&md5=920b502aff006247853fb5f9598264bc).

**Anne Fletcher** (born May 1, 1966) is an American choreographer, film director, dancer and actress. She directed the films _[Step Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_(film) "Step Up (film)")_ (2006), _[27 Dresses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/27\_Dresses "27 Dresses")_ (2008), _[The Proposal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Proposal\_(2009\_film) "The Proposal (2009 film)")_ (2009), _[The Guilt Trip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guilt\_Trip\_(film) "The Guilt Trip (film)")_ (2012), _[Hot Pursuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot\_Pursuit\_(2015\_film) "Hot Pursuit (2015 film)")_ (2015), _[Dumplin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dumplin'\_(film) "Dumplin' (film)")_ (2018), and _[Hocus Pocus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hocus\_Pocus\_2 "Hocus Pocus 2")_ (2022).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anne_Fletcher&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Born **Anne Marie Fletcher** in Detroit, [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan"), Fletcher lived with her family in the local lakefront suburb of [St. Clair Shores, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Clair_Shores,_Michigan "St. Clair Shores, Michigan") until her 1984 graduation with honors from [Lake Shore High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Shore_High_School "Lake Shore High School").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-:0-1) Fletcher began taking dance lessons at a local dance studio, Turning Point School of the Performing Arts, at age 12 after watching her mother take a dance class. At age 15, she appeared in the local show _Salute to the Superstars_ at the now-defunct Mr. F's Beef & Bourbon dinner club in [Sterling Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling_Heights "Sterling Heights"), [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan"). Upon graduation from high school, Fletcher moved to Los Angeles, California, where she received further training from renowned choreographer [Joe Tremaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Tremaine "Joe Tremaine"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-2) and began working as a professional dancer; including performing as a [Laker Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laker_Girls "Laker Girls").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-:0-1)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anne_Fletcher&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Choreographic career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anne_Fletcher&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Choreographic career")]

In 1990, Fletcher met [Adam Shankman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Shankman "Adam Shankman") when they were hired to perform as dancers at the [62nd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/62nd_Academy_Awards "62nd Academy Awards"). Shortly thereafter, Shankman hired Fletcher to become his assistant choreographer. This sparked a longtime personal friendship and professional affiliation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-3)

Fletcher worked closely with Shankman both during his career as a choreographer and later as a film director and has credited her collaborations with Shankman for allowing her to both develop her own set of choreographic and film directorial skills and to achieve a similarly successful career path.

In her first film roles, Fletcher appeared as a dancer, including _[The Flintstones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flintstones\_(film) "The Flintstones (film)")_ (1994), _[The Mask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mask\_(1994\_film) "The Mask (1994 film)")_ (1994), _[Tank Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tank\_Girl\_(film) "Tank Girl (film)")_ (1995), _[Casper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casper\_(film) "Casper (film)")_ (1995) and _[Titanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanic\_(1997\_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")_ (1997). Fletcher later developed choreography for the Oscar-nominated drama film _[Boogie Nights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boogie\_Nights "Boogie Nights")_ (1997) starring [Mark Wahlberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Wahlberg "Mark Wahlberg"), [Burt Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Reynolds "Burt Reynolds"), [Julianne Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julianne_Moore "Julianne Moore") and [Heather Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heather_Graham "Heather Graham"), in which she also appeared as a dancer, as well as for the comedy film _[A Life Less Ordinary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Life\_Less\_Ordinary "A Life Less Ordinary")_ (1997) with [Ewan McGregor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ewan_McGregor "Ewan McGregor") and [Cameron Diaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz "Cameron Diaz").

### Directorial career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anne_Fletcher&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Directorial career")]

After acquiring numerous professional choreography credits, often in collaboration with Adam Shankman, Fletcher, with encouragement from Shankman, began to consider a directorial career. She worked alongside Shankman, who himself had moved from choreography to directing with films such as _[Hairspray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hairspray\_(2007\_film) "Hairspray (2007 film)")_ (2007) and _[The Wedding Planner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wedding\_Planner "The Wedding Planner")_, for both of which she was an associate producer,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-:1-4) as well as _[Step Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_(film) "Step Up (film)")_.

Although Fletcher began to break into the production side of filmmaking throughout the early 2000s, she continued to choreograph in films such as the _[Ice Princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice\_Princess "Ice Princess")_ and _[The Pacifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pacifier "The Pacifier")_ in 2005.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-:2-5) She also did choreograph work in other films like _[Scooby-Doo 2: Monsters Unleashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scooby-Doo\_2:\_Monsters\_Unleashed "Scooby-Doo 2: Monsters Unleashed")_ (2004), _[The 40-Year-Old Virgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_40-Year-Old\_Virgin "The 40-Year-Old Virgin")_ (2005) and _[Hairspray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hairspray\_(2007\_film) "Hairspray (2007 film)")_ (2007).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-:2-5)

Fletcher directed the 2006 romantic dance film, _Step Up_ starring [Channing Tatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channing_Tatum "Channing Tatum") and [Jenna Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan "Jenna Dewan"). The film was nominated for two [Teen Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_Choice_Awards "Teen Choice Awards") (2007) and one [Young Artist Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Artist_Award "Young Artist Award") (2007). Fletcher turned down the offer to direct the sequel to this film, fearing that if she directed another dance film, she would not be able to branch out into other genres in the future.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-6) Although she did the choreography on _[Step Up 2: The Streets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step\_Up\_2:\_The\_Streets "Step Up 2: The Streets")_ (2008), the role of director was given to [Jon M. Chu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_M._Chu "Jon M. Chu"). Panned by critics, the film was well-received by audiences and grossed $65 million at the domestic box office.

Her work on _Step Up_ earned Fletcher a second successful director credit on the popular 2008 romantic comedy film, _[27 Dresses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/27\_Dresses "27 Dresses")_, starring [Katherine Heigl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katherine_Heigl "Katherine Heigl") and [James Marsden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Marsden "James Marsden"). This film was nominated for eight awards: one [People's Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Awards "People's Choice Awards") (2008), two [Teen Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_Choice_Awards "Teen Choice Awards") (2008), three [Golden Trailer Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Trailer_Awards "Golden Trailer Awards") (2008), one [Artios Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artios_Award "Artios Award") (2008) and one _EDA Special Mention Award._ 27 Dresses is celebrated as an iconic 21st-century romantic comedy film, thanks in large part to Fletcher's directing. Former president of MGM Jonathan Glickman emphasized how important Fletcher was to the success of the film, stating that she and the main character are very similar people. The writer of the film, Aline Brosh McKenna, mentioned in an interview that Fletcher was known on set as "Mama", and credits her for capturing the story so well.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-7)

Based on the success of her first two features, Fletcher went on to direct the popular 2009 romantic comedy film, [_The Proposal_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Proposal_(2009_film) "The Proposal (2009 film)"), starring [Sandra Bullock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandra_Bullock "Sandra Bullock") and [Ryan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Reynolds "Ryan Reynolds"). This film was nominated for twenty-seven awards; out of the twenty-seven nominations, the film won seven. For her performance, Bullock received a Golden Globe nomination for best actress and a Women's Image Network Award for Outstanding Actress.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-8) The Proposal is Fletcher's highest-grossing film as a director, and it stands as the 7th highest grossing romantic comedy of all time.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-9)

Following the success of _The Proposal_, Fletcher directed [_The Guilt Trip_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guilt_Trip_(film) "The Guilt Trip (film)") (2012) starring [Seth Rogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Rogen "Seth Rogen") and [Barbra Streisand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbra_Streisand "Barbra Streisand"). She followed this by directing [_Hot Pursuit_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Pursuit_(2015_film) "Hot Pursuit (2015 film)") (2015) starring [Reese Witherspoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reese_Witherspoon "Reese Witherspoon") and [Sofía Vergara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sof%C3%ADa_Vergara "Sofía Vergara"). Both of these films performed significantly worse than her previous films, with the former receiving only one [Razzie Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Razzie_Award "Razzie Award") nomination[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-10) and the latter earning an 8% on Rotten Tomatoes.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-11)

In July 2014, Fletcher was announced as director for _[Disenchanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disenchanted\_(film) "Disenchanted (film)")_, the sequel to the 2007 film starring Amy Adams and Patrick Dempsey. However, in October 2016, she was replaced by her friend Adam Shankman.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-13)

In December 2018, Fletcher released [Dumplin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dumplin'_(film) "Dumplin' (film)"), her first film released exclusively on Netflix. The film is based on the book of the same name, and stars Jennifer Aniston as a former beauty queen. The film grapples with issues related to body positivity and mother-daughter relationships.

Fletcher directed _[Hocus Pocus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hocus\_Pocus\_2 "Hocus Pocus 2")_, the 2022 sequel to _[Hocus Pocus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hocus\_Pocus\_(1993\_film) "Hocus Pocus (1993 film)")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-14) The film was released exclusively on Disney+ and stars Sarah Jessica Parker, Bette Midler, and Kathy Najimy as the Sanderson Sisters from the 1993 original film.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-15) The film was polarized by critics, but received two [Kids' Choice Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kids'_Choice_Award "Kids' Choice Award") nominations, including [Favorite Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kids'_Choice_Award_for_Favorite_Movie "Kids' Choice Award for Favorite Movie") (losing to _[Sonic the Hedgehog 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonic\_the\_Hedgehog\_2\_(film) "Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (film)")_). She will reprise her role as director on the upcoming _Hocus Pocus 3_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Fletcher#cite_note-16)

# Trivia

## Hocus Pocus 2

Edit

On the podcast [Inside of You with Michael Rosenbaum (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt12239824/?ref_=tttrv_tr), [Doug Jones](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0427964/?ref_=tttrv_tr) said that the wig he wears as Billy Butcherson in this movie is the same one he wore in the first movie.

Helpful•482 6

[Bette Midler](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000541/?ref_=tttrv_tr) is largely responsible for Hocus Pocus 2 becoming a reality. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly, Bette stated that when she started to realize how popular the original film had become, she "was surprised" and "started making calls". After going online, she stated, "I'd never seen so much Hocus Pocus merch." She says she realized something was going on. "As I watched it progress, I'd call the studio once a year to ask, 'How about it?'"

Helpful•567 10

In the original film, Mary's mouth is crooked to the right. This time, it's to the left. [Kathy Najimy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001562/?ref_=tttrv_tr) has disclosed that this is because it's hard for her to do it on the original side now. The movie explains the change away by having Winifred slap Mary, making her mouth move to the other side.

Helpful•419 7

During the scene when the mayor loses his place in line, the couple sitting on the bench are dressed as a devil and an old lady with hair rollers. This is a callback to the original [Garry Marshall](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005190/?ref_=tttrv_tr) and [Penny Marshall](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001508/?ref_=tttrv_tr) roles as the unsuspecting married couple who host the sisters for an evening.

Helpful•362 6

Maiden, Mother, and Crone are referenced in the incantation spell. Also known as "The Triple Goddess", these entities together form a deity or deity archetype revered in many Neopagan religious and spiritual traditions. In common Neopagan usage, the Triple Goddess is viewed as a triunity of three distinct aspects or figures united in one being. The Sanderson Sisters themselves embody these figures - Winifred is the Crone, Mary the Mother, and Sarah the Maiden.

**Kenneth John Ortega** ([/ɔːr ˈ t eɪ ɡ ə/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_or-TAY-gə_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born April 18, 1950) is an American director, producer, choreographer, and concert creator. He is best known for his work with [Disney Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel "Disney Channel"), notably the _[High School Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_School\_Musical\_(franchise) "High School Musical (franchise)")_ film trilogy, cult classics such as _[Newsies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsies "Newsies")_ and _[Hocus Pocus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hocus\_Pocus\_(1993\_film) "Hocus Pocus (1993 film)")_, _[The Cheetah Girls 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cheetah\_Girls\_2 "The Cheetah Girls 2")_, and the first three _[Descendants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descendants\_(franchise) "Descendants (franchise)")_ films. In 2019, he signed a five year deal with [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), producing the original series _[Julie and the Phantoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie\_and\_the\_Phantoms "Julie and the Phantoms"),_ which was cancelled after only one season. He has also choreographed multiple iconic 1980s films such as _[Xanadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xanadu\_(film) "Xanadu (film)")_, _[One from the Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One\_from\_the\_Heart "One from the Heart")_, _[St. Elmo's Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St.\_Elmo's\_Fire\_(film) "St. Elmo's Fire (film)")_, _[Pretty in Pink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty\_in\_Pink "Pretty in Pink")_, _[Ferris Bueller's Day Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris\_Bueller's\_Day\_Off "Ferris Bueller's Day Off")_, and _[Dirty Dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty\_Dancing "Dirty Dancing")._ Ortega has worked on multiple music videos and produced concert tours for the likes of [Kiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_(band) "Kiss (band)"), [Olivia Newton-John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Newton-John "Olivia Newton-John"), [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher "Cher"), [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna"), [Miley Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miley_Cyrus "Miley Cyrus"), and [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"), notably the cancelled [This is It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_It_(concert_residency) "This Is It (concert residency)") concert residency. He also wrote, directed, and produced Jackson's posthumous documentary film, _[Michael Jackson's This Is It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael\_Jackson's\_This\_Is\_It "Michael Jackson's This Is It")_. For his work, Ortega was honored with a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") and a [Disney Legend Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Legends "Disney Legends") in 2019.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-2)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Ortega&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Ortega was born in [Palo Alto, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California "Palo Alto, California"), the son of Madeline, a waitress, and Octavio "Tibby" Ortega, a factory worker. He also has a sister, Debra Ortega and brother, Mark Ortega. Both of his parents were also born in Palo Alto,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-elc-3) though his paternal grandparents were Spanish immigrants.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-4) He attended [Sequoia High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequoia_High_School_(Redwood_City,_California) "Sequoia High School (Redwood City, California)") in [Redwood City, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redwood_City,_California "Redwood City, California"), where he was a cheerleader and in the drama group.

Ortega began his career as an actor, appearing in a touring production of _[Oliver!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver! "Oliver!")_ and [_Hair_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_(musical) "Hair (musical)") before venturing into choreography and directing. Ortega choreographed [The Mystic Knights of the Oingo Boingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mystic_Knights_of_the_Oingo_Boingo "The Mystic Knights of the Oingo Boingo") in the mid to late 1970s.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Ortega was offered the leading role in a production of _[Jesus Christ Superstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus\_Christ\_Superstar "Jesus Christ Superstar"),_ but turned the offer down to become a choreographer for the San Francisco-based band [The Tubes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tubes "The Tubes") after being spotted on the dance floor in a club by members of the band. Ortega toured with the band for ten years, before being contracted by [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher "Cher") to choreograph a TV special and tour and by [Kiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_(band) "Kiss (band)") on their [Dynasty Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynasty_Tour "Dynasty Tour").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-variety.com-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-6)

In 1980, Ortega was hired as one of the choreographers on the film _[Xanadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xanadu\_(film) "Xanadu (film)")_, working with [Gene Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Kelly "Gene Kelly") who mentored him into choreographing for film. During this time period, Ortega also served as choreographer for several of [John Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hughes_(filmmaker) "John Hughes (filmmaker)")'s films, including _[Pretty in Pink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty\_in\_Pink "Pretty in Pink")_ and _[Ferris Bueller's Day Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris\_Bueller's\_Day\_Off "Ferris Bueller's Day Off")_, as well as the 1987 film _[Dirty Dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty\_Dancing "Dirty Dancing")_.

Ortega would also choreograph several music videos, including "[Material Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Material_Girl "Material Girl")" by [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna_(entertainer) "Madonna (entertainer)"), "[She's a Beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She's_a_Beauty "She's a Beauty")" by The Tubes, [Physical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_(Olivia_Newton-John_song) "Physical (Olivia Newton-John song)") by [Olivia Newton-John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Newton-John "Olivia Newton-John") and "[Mr. Roboto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Roboto "Mr. Roboto")" by [Styx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Styx_(band) "Styx (band)"). He also produced and choreographed the video for "[Rock Me Tonite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Me_Tonite "Rock Me Tonite")" by [Billy Squier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Squier "Billy Squier"), which turned into a career-ending disaster for the artist.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-7)

He made his directorial debut in 1992 with the [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney") musical _[Newsies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsies "Newsies")_, which was followed up by [_Hocus Pocus_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hocus_Pocus_(1993_film) "Hocus Pocus (1993 film)") in 1993. Both films underperformed at the box-office but have since gone on to attract considerable cult followings. Ortega also served as choreographer for _[To Wong Foo, Thanks for Everything! Julie Newmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_Wong\_Foo,\_Thanks\_for\_Everything!\_Julie\_Newmar "To Wong Foo, Thanks for Everything! Julie Newmar")_ in 1995.

Alongside [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson"), he created and designed Jackson's [Dangerous World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_World_Tour "Dangerous World Tour") (1992–1993), [HIStory World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIStory_World_Tour "HIStory World Tour") (1996–1997) and [Michael Jackson & Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson_&_Friends "Michael Jackson & Friends") (1999). He has also choreographed events ranging from [Super Bowl XXX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXX "Super Bowl XXX"), the [72nd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/72nd_Academy_Awards "72nd Academy Awards"), the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") ([Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta")) and the [2002 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Winter_Olympics "2002 Winter Olympics") ([Salt Lake City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Lake_City "Salt Lake City")).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-8)

In 2006, Ortega directed and choreographed two [Disney Channel Original Movies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Disney_Channel_original_films "List of Disney Channel original films"), _[High School Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_School\_Musical "High School Musical")_ and _[The Cheetah Girls 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cheetah\_Girls\_2 "The Cheetah Girls 2")_. Ortega would return as director and choreographer for _[High School Musical 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_School\_Musical\_2 "High School Musical 2")_ in 2007 and _[High School Musical 3: Senior Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_School\_Musical\_3:\_Senior\_Year "High School Musical 3: Senior Year")_ in 2008.

In April 2009, Ortega began work directing and choreographing the scheduled 50-date Michael Jackson [This Is It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Is_It_(concert_residency) "This Is It (concert residency)") concert residency at [the O2 Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_O2_Arena "The O2 Arena"), billed as Jackson's final concerts in London.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-9) The engagement was subsequently cancelled due to [Jackson's sudden death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Michael_Jackson "Death of Michael Jackson") on June 25, 2009.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-10) Ortega would serve as the director of the Michael Jackson Public Memorial at the Staples Center in Los Angeles, which was broadcast live on several networks on July 7, 2009, reaching a television audience of 31 million in America and more than one billion worldwide.

At the end of the service, he introduced a rendition of Jackson's 1985 charity single "[We Are the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_the_World "We Are the World")" created for the This Is It concerts, featuring Jackson's backing singers on lead vocals with his dancers performing around them. Ortega directed the concert film _[Michael Jackson's This Is It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael\_Jackson's\_This\_Is\_It "Michael Jackson's This Is It")_, which was put together from rehearsal footage recorded at the [Los Angeles Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Forum "Los Angeles Forum") and the [Staples Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center"). The film was released on October 28 of the same year.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-12)

He was set to direct the 2011 _[Footloose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Footloose\_(2011\_film) "Footloose (2011 film)")_ remake, but dropped out in October 2009 due to differences with [Paramount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") over the budget and tone of the film.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-13)

Ortega was also hired to direct a film adaptation of the [Broadway musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_musical "Broadway musical")_[In the Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_the\_Heights "In the Heights")_ for [Universal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures "Universal Pictures"), but the studio dropped the project in 2011 due to budgetary and casting issues.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-14) On August 9, 2011, it was announced that Ortega would direct a remake of _[Dirty Dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty\_Dancing\_(2017\_film) "Dirty Dancing (2017 film)")_, a project that was later postponed. The [2017 TV remake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty_Dancing_(2017_film) "Dirty Dancing (2017 film)") was filmed without Ortega's involvement.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-15)

On May 12, 2014, Ortega guest-judged on the [18th season of _Dancing with the Stars_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_with_the_Stars_(American_season_18) "Dancing with the Stars (American season 18)") during the [semifinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_with_the_Stars_(U.S._season_18)#Week_9:_American_Icons_Night_.28Semifinals.29 "Dancing with the Stars (U.S. season 18)").

In 2015, Ortega directed and choreographed _[Descendants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descendants\_(2015\_film) "Descendants (2015 film)")_ for the Disney Channel, a film based on the children of legendary [Disney Villains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Villains "Disney Villains"). He would return in the same capacity for its two sequels, _[Descendants 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descendants\_2 "Descendants 2")_ in 2017 and _[Descendants 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descendants\_3 "Descendants 3")_ in 2019.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-16)

In 2019, Ortega was honored with a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") and was named a [Disney Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Legend "Disney Legend") at the 2019 [D23 Expo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D23_Expo "D23 Expo").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-18)

That fall, he directed and served as executive producer of the Netflix Original series _[Julie and the Phantoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie\_and\_the\_Phantoms "Julie and the Phantoms")_, which premiered on Netflix on September 10, 2020.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Ortega&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Ortega is [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_men "Gay men"), and in a 2014 interview with anti-bullying organization [Bystander Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bystander_Revolution "Bystander Revolution"), he said that "as a gay man having grown up in the 50s and 60s, I have to say, I'm very proud of the industry that I work in," referring to the acceptance of people with different sexual orientations in show business.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-19)

During the trial _[People v. Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_v.\_Murray "People v. Murray")_ regarding the [death of Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Michael_Jackson "Death of Michael Jackson"), Ortega was the trial's first witness.

In 2020, Ortega recalled being falsely arrested at the age of 21 after a chief of police planted narcotics in his hotel room, allegedly upset by his performance in a touring production of _Hair_. The charges were dropped after investigations were made and Ortega recalled the arrest report identifying him as George Berger, the name of the character he played in the show.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Ortega#cite_note-variety.com-5)

Bryce Dallas Howard (born March 2, 1981) is an American actress and director. Howard is the daughter of filmmaker Ron Howard and writer Cheryl Howard. She attended the New York University Tisch School of the Arts, left in 2002 to take roles on Broadway but graduated in 2020. While portraying Rosalind in a 2003 production of As You Like It, Howard caught the attention of director M. Night Shyamalan, who cast her as a blind girl in the thriller The Village (2004). She later secured the starring role of a naiad in Shyamalan's fantasy film Lady in the Water (2006). Howard's performance in Kenneth Branagh's As You Like It (2006) earned her a Golden Globe Award nomination and she subsequently appeared as Gwen Stacy in Sam Raimi's superhero film Spider-Man 3 (2007). She went on to appear as Kate Connor in the action film Terminator Salvation (2009) and as Victoria in the fantasy film The Twilight Saga: Eclipse (2010). These along with her roles as a "fair-weather" girlfriend in the comedy-drama 50/50 (2011) and as a racist socialite in the period-drama The Help (2011) brought her increased recognition. Howard emerged a star with her role as Claire Dearing in the top-grossing Jurassic World trilogy (2015–2022). She also portrayed a forest ranger in the adventure film Pete's Dragon (2016); Sheila Dwight, Elton John's mother, in the biopic Rocketman (2019); and voiced Yaddle in an episode of Tales of the Jedi (2022). Howard directed the documentary Dads (2019), and episodes of the Disney+ space western series The Mandalorian (2019–present) and The Book of Boba Fett (2022). She is married to actor Seth Gabel, with whom she has two children.

 #### [5. Stephen King](link_69) 

    *   Writer
    *   Producer
    *   Actor

[Maximum Overdrive (1986)](link_70)

Stephen Edwin King was born on September 21, 1947, at the Maine General Hospital in Portland. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname "Pollock," but used the last name "King," under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.  
  
Stephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named "Dave's Rag". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called "People, Places, and Things--Volume I". King's stories included "Hotel at the End of the Road", "I've Got to Get Away!", "The Dimension Warp", "The Thing at the Bottom of the Well", "The Stranger", "I'm Falling", "The Cursed Expedition", and "The Other Side of the Fog." A year later, King's amateur press, Triad and Gaslight Books, published a two-part book titled "The Star Invaders".  
  
King made his first actual published appearance in 1965 in the magazine Comics Review with his story "I Was a Teenage Grave Robber." The story ran about 6,000 words in length. In 1966 he graduated from high school and took a scholarship to attend the University of Maine. Looking back on his high school days, King recalled that "my high school career was totally undistinguished. I was not at the top of my class, nor at the bottom." Later that summer King began working on a novel called "Getting It On", about some kids who take over a classroom and try unsuccessfully to ward off the National Guard. During his first year at college, King completed his first full-length novel, "The Long Walk." He submitted the novel to [Bennett Cerf](link_71)/Random House only to have it rejected. King took the rejection badly and filed the book away.  
  
He made his first small sale--$35--with the story "The Glass Floor". In June 1970 King graduated from the University of Maine with a Bachelor of Science degree in English and a certificate to teach high school. King's next idea came from the poem by [Robert Browning](link_72), "Childe Roland to the Dark Tower Came." He found bright colored green paper in the library and began work on "The Dark Tower" saga, but his chronic shortage of money meant that he was unable to further pursue the novel, and it, too, was filed away. King took a job at a filling station pumping gas for the princely sum of $1.25 an hour. Soon he began to earn money for his writings by submitting his short stories to men's magazines such as Cavalier.  
  
On January 2, 1971, he married [Tabitha King](link_73) (born Tabitha Jane Spruce). In the fall of 1971 King took a teaching job at Hampden Academy, earning $6,400 a year. The Kings then moved to Hermon, a town west of Bangor. Stephen then began work on a short story about a teenage girl named Carietta White. After completing a few pages, he decided it was not a worthy story and crumpled the pages up and tossed them into the trash. Fortunately, Tabitha took the pages out and read them. She encouraged her husband to continue the story, which he did. In January 1973 he submitted "Carrie" to Doubleday. In March Doubleday bought the book. On May 12 the publisher sold the paperback rights for the novel to New American Library for $400,000. His contract called for his getting half of that sum, and he quit his teaching job to pursue writing full time. The rest, as they say, is history.  
  
Since then King has had numerous short stories and novels published and movies made from his work. He has been called the "Master of Horror". His books have been translated into 33 different languages, published in over 35 different countries. There are over 300 million copies of his novels in publication. He continues to live in Bangor, Maine, with his wife, and writes out of his home.  
  
In June 1999 King was severely injured in an accident, he was walking alongside a highway and was hit by a van, that left him in critical condition with injuries to his lung, broken ribs, a broken leg and a severely fractured hip. After three weeks of operations, he was released from the Central Maine Medical Center in Lewiston.

Nicholas Sparks was born on December 31, 1965 in Omaha, Nebraska. He graduated from the University of Notre Dame in 1988 and is one of the more critically-acclaimed authors of the past 5 years. He is the author of 5 best-selling books, including "The Notebook" and "The Rescue". Eleven of his books, [Message in a Bottle (1999)](link_51), [A Walk to Remember (2002)](link_52), [The Notebook (2004)](link_53), [Nights in Rodanthe (2008)](link_54), The Last Song [2010] , Dear John [2010] , The Lucky One [2012], Safe Haven [2013] , The Best of Me [2014] , [The Longest Ride (2015)](link_55) and [The Choice (2016)](link_56)  
  
have been adapted into blockbuster movies. Sparks lives in North Carolina with his wife, 3 sons, and twin daughters.

Markdown Content:
Log in

![Image 1: Muse](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/brand/muse-logo.svg)
# Muse, AI that gets it done for you Muse[Video 1](https://l.facebook.com/videos/avatars/hatch_connecting.mp4)[Video 2](https://l.facebook.com/videos/avatars/hatch_working.mp4), AI that gets it done for you sorts your email books reservations shops for you saves you money manages calendars builds fitness plans gets it done for you sorts your email![Image 2](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-envelope.webp)books reservations![Image 3](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-airplane.webp)shops for you![Image 4](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-cart.webp)saves you money![Image 5](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-piggybank.webp)manages calendars![Image 6](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/icon-calendar.webp)builds fitness plans![Image 7](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/icons/b-01.webp)gets it done for you

# Log in or create an account

Mobile number or email(required) 

You may receive SMS notifications from us by using your mobile number. [Learn more](https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/31983416211257755/)

Continue

[Learn more](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https://muse.ai/&h=AUDHaxY9pE2rUPl2Vx_EjPFIU-qVBtDu4n716Lpp1uT7tp41S9_RmsgBapJzXcRzz-xt-CnimX2i29zRfclux1RHaST__mFshy_sbuFtQaaZdcabozAOgLbGNiRHH3G6SBwN4T5yZJOLOQ#landing-introduction-video-title)

## Built around your whole life

Give Muse a goal or task and it handles the rest, from saving money and improving your health to smart shopping and helping you strengthen your relationships.

[Video 3](https://scontent.xx.fbcdn.net/o1/v/t6/f2/m421/AQPvdntV2G814fVexG62mHy9MLAFz-IUx2_276pwlTOScjlG7403bT1NxrxgW2yToPZR5BOsHoRWgC3EQGGX.mp4?_nc_sid=9c7e41&_nc_ht=scontent.xx.fbcdn.net&ccb=17-1&_nc_gid=TVsKELabZkGAExMM87CdOg&edm=AIlawRcEAAAA&_nc_zt=28&oh=00_AQN7fADER8eZwvQcApr_CYb1qQT9LGzx2qtIvYp3ElCv3Q&oe=6AE9AEEE#t=1)

### Every Muse user shares their own computer in the cloud with their Muse.

Muse Secure VM is a persistent, isolated Linux computer with a full browser that you and your agent can use to complete tasks, allowing you to intervene at any point. It's your computer and your browser, with the storage, CPU, and memory to handle real work.

![Image 8: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/browser.webp)![Image 9: Floating browser, search, map, calendar, and confirmation panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/browser-dark.webp)

### Designed around the way you already communicate

Chat with your agent in the same way you message with other people, using the Muse app on mobile, Mac, or directly in WhatsApp. There's no learning curve, just tell Muse what you want to get done.

![Image 10: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/messaging.webp)![Image 11: A chat on a phone where the agent has filled out a school form, shown beside a laptop](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/messaging-dark.webp)

### Stay in control of what your agent does

Approve actions your agent takes on your behalf before they happen, like sending emails and making purchases. See a complete audit trail of everything your agent has done (and what it's planning to do).

![Image 12: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/approvals.webp)![Image 13: Floating purchase, message, activity, permission, and decision controls](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/approvals-dark.webp)

### Your data is kept secure and private

Save your logins to a secure credential store Muse can't see, with 1Password integration coming soon. When shopping, a one-time card number is generated at checkout so your real card stays hidden from the merchant and your agent. Eligible purchases are covered by [Link's purchase protections](https://link.com/protections), a first for AI agents, and your conversations are not shared with Meta's ad systems.

![Image 14: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/secure-storage.webp)![Image 15: A vault, privacy shield, masked credential, security control, and virtual card](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/secure-storage-dark.webp)

### Proactively helps with your goals and suggests ideas

Muse helps you stay on top of things, takes tasks and projects off your plate, and turns long-term goals into real progress. It learns from conversations, reflects on what matters and gets sharper, coming back with ideas built around what you actually need, ready to act on them under your direction.

![Image 16: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/goals.webp)![Image 17: Floating checklist, calendar, route, progress, and idea panels](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/goals-dark.webp)

### Connects to your apps and builds its own tools

Connect the apps you use daily, like email, calendar, and Instagram. You decide what your agent can see and what it can do. If a task needs a tool that doesn't exist, your agent builds it for you.

![Image 18: Connected app, messaging, media, cloud, calendar, and automation tiles](https://l.facebook.com/images/landing/connectors.webp)

## Get the most out of your Muse

A guided tour of Muse, from setting a first goal to seeing it through.

![Image 19: Product designer presenting a guided tour of Muse](https://l.facebook.com/images/hatch/landing/product-walkthrough-cover.png)

## Learn more about Muse

Explore the choices behind Muse and how it is built to deserve your trust.

### [How We Designed Muse When Muse works, it feels like magic. These are the product choices that make the experience possible.](https://introducing.muse.ai/)### [How We Built Safety Into Muse Muse is built for privacy, safety, and security. Learn how these principles shape every part of the product.](https://security.muse.ai/)### [Muse for Business Meet the AI agent that works for your small business and keeps jobs moving between your decisions.](https://l.facebook.com/business)

## Ready to try Muse?

Log in

Bryce Dallas Howard (born March 2, 1981) is an American actress and director. Howard is the daughter of filmmaker Ron Howard and writer Cheryl Howard. She attended the New York University Tisch School of the Arts, left in 2002 to take roles on Broadway but graduated in 2020. While portraying Rosalind in a 2003 production of As You Like It, Howard caught the attention of director M. Night Shyamalan, who cast her as a blind girl in the thriller The Village (2004). She later secured the starring role of a naiad in Shyamalan's fantasy film Lady in the Water (2006). Howard's performance in Kenneth Branagh's As You Like It (2006) earned her a Golden Globe Award nomination and she subsequently appeared as Gwen Stacy in Sam Raimi's superhero film Spider-Man 3 (2007). She went on to appear as Kate Connor in the action film Terminator Salvation (2009) and as Victoria in the fantasy film The Twilight Saga: Eclipse (2010). These along with her roles as a "fair-weather" girlfriend in the comedy-drama 50/50 (2011) and as a racist socialite in the period-drama The Help (2011) brought her increased recognition. Howard emerged a star with her role as Claire Dearing in the top-grossing Jurassic World trilogy (2015–2022). She also portrayed a forest ranger in the adventure film Pete's Dragon (2016); Sheila Dwight, Elton John's mother, in the biopic Rocketman (2019); and voiced Yaddle in an episode of Tales of the Jedi (2022). Howard directed the documentary Dads (2019), and episodes of the Disney+ space western series The Mandalorian (2019–present) and The Book of Boba Fett (2022). She is married to actor Seth Gabel, with whom she has two children.

## [Technical Achievement Award](https://www.imdb.com/oscars/event/ev0000003/2026/1/?ref_=fea_eds_top-1_2#technical_achievement_award)

[Edit](https://contribute.imdb.com/updates/edit?ref_=ev_csegosc_edt&edit=ev0000003%3Ayear%7E2026)

*   
Winner  
    *   [Marc Specter](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2986501/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)

For the design and development of the Kraken Dialogue Editors Toolkit, enabling precise audio assembly. With an intuitive user interface and transcription utility that provides audio asset management, enabling direct access to edit decision lists and audio session files, Kraken expedites the assembly of audio files while providing visual aids to find and resolve issues.

*   
![Image 132: Paul Debevec](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BNjAzOTM5OGEtOGUyNS00MmM4LWI3ZWQtNDhhZWQ1MzIwMjAxXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1663206/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)    

Winner  
    *   [Paul Debevec](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1663206/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)

For his pioneering work in high dynamic range, image-based lighting techniques. Debevec demonstrated the advantages of high dynamic range image-based lighting, and, through advocacy of the approach, led the industry to embrace new workflows. This has enabled artists to work more productively and improved the realism of computer graphics imagery in feature films.

*   
Winner  
    *   [Andrea Weidlich](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm6942275/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)

For her research on layered materials and implementation of the layering operators and BSDFs in Weta FX's Manuka renderer. Weidlich's research and the methods underlying Manuka's layered material system have been influential across the visual effects industry and have allowed Weta FX to raise the bar for photorealism.

*   
Winner  
    *   [Justin Webster](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1383714/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)

For the design and engineering of Matchbox, a system for audio and video matching that enables auto-reconform. Providing detailed insight into differences between audio and video files, even in the absence of metadata, Matchbox enables rapid application of changes in post-production while preserving previous creative work.

*   
![Image 133: Luca Fascione](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BYTA0ZmUyYzEtYmNiOC00MmRhLTgwZTctYWYyY2ZiZWNjYWMzXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UY60_CR12,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4540822/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)    

Winner  
    *   [Luca Fascione](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4540822/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)

For the initial design and development of the layered materials system at Weta FX. The Manuka renderer's efficient and flexible system for layering materials has unlocked workflows that have allowed Weta FX to scale to ever-larger productions while giving artists both creative freedom and physical accuracy.

*   
Winner  
    *   [Jonathan Moulin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4181522/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)

For the design and creative vision, of Lama at Industrial Light & Magic. Lama provides an artist-friendly approach to composing materials built from layers representing distinct physical phenomena. Its modular, carefully curated design allows look development artists to create unique, physically plausible appearances without writing shader code. Its ease of use has expanded and accelerated shading workflows at Industrial Light & Magic and led to broader industry adoption via its inclusion in Pixar's RenderMan.

*   
Winner  
    *   [Emmanuel Turquin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm14852217/?ref_=ev_csegosc_nom)

For the design, architecture and engineering of Lama at Industrial Light & Magic. Lama provides an artist-friendly approach to composing materials built from layers representing distinct physical phenomena. ## WELCOME TO REFRAME 2023!

From the heart of Nogojiwanong/Peterborough, we are thrilled to announce ReFrame’s 2023 festival season will once again be available online across Canada! The 19th edition of the festival will offer on-demand viewing of over 60 films from the comfort of home**January 26th to February 3rd, 2023**.

ReFrame will give audiences from coast to coast to coast a full nine days to stream films, panels, special events and more! Although 2023 will be mostly virtual, we’ll be hosting limited in-person events during the festival including an opening night event at Showplace Performance Centre. The virtual platform continues to provide an audience experience that is safe, convenient and accessible.
